description: Refactor the existing Model Creation Flow to keep the current four-step user experience while separating model training, evaluation, fine-tuning, and final model persistence. Training and fine-tuning must not commit the model to the database. The model is persisted only when the user explicitly clicks Save Model in Step 4.
progress_note: 2026-09-01: MODEL-FLOW-014 added (train/test split distribution panel + honest seed control) — denominator moves 14 -> 15, so the completed-count percentage drops from 57 to 53 (8/15) with no work regressing, the same convention every prior pass in this note uses. …

draft_persistence.chosen: B — ModelDraft as a database entity
draft_persistence.rationale: A training container has no browser: it authenticates with a run token hashed into a row, reads its spec from /claim, and writes logs and metrics back over HTTP. A client-only jotai draft (MODEL-FLOW-002 as built) is unreachable from that process, so training could not run against it at all. Mirrors DatasetDraft (DS-LAKE-005), which solved the identical problem for the dataset wizard and is already proven in production — including the abandon-not-delete rule and the adopt-by-pointer save.

rejected.A — nullable modelId on ModelTrainingRun: Would work, but leaves the draft's own configuration (name, location, dataset, algorithm, target, split) with nowhere server-side to live, so Step 4's Save Model would still have to trust a client-supplied config. DatasetDraft exists precisely to avoid that.
rejected.C — create Model at training, flip statu: Directly contradicts the global definition of done. Also leaks: an abandoned wizard leaves a Model row in the workspace listing.

persistence_boundary_clarified.note: 'No database commit before Save Model' means no persistent MODEL record. It does not mean no writes at all. ModelDraft, ModelTrainingRun, ModelTrainingRunLog and ModelFineTuningJob are all written before Save Model — they are job and workspace rows, the same class of row PreprocessingJob and DatasetArtifact occupy during the dataset wizard, where DS-LAKE-005 already accepted them. What Save Model creates is the Model itself, and it adopts everything else by pointer.

artifact_scope.note: Run outputs are written under drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/, not models/{modelId}/runs/{runId}/ — a modelId does not exist when the container uploads. Save Model adopts those objects by pointer (never copies bytes), the same rule DatasetArtifact.datasetId's own schema comment states. is_model_run_key/model_run_key must accept the draft scope; see MODEL-FLOW-006-T07.

fine_tuning_undefined.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-25, user decision. This ledger's own guess above turned out right: 'fine-tuning' = a hyperparameter search — one algorithm, one artifact, one train/test split, N hyperparameter sets tried in sequence, best kept by RMSE (not R² — see MODEL-FLOW-005's own implementation note for why). Not fine-tuning in the transfer-learning sense, and not a retrain on different/widened data — that reading was explicitly considered and rejected. MODEL-FLOW-005 built 2026-08-25 on this definition; T01-T08 there are no longer speculative. MODEL-SERVE-004 (/retrain) is the SAME question under decisions.retrain_and_fine_tuning_are_one_question and is NOT auto-unblocked by this note — whoever picks it up applies this same answer there and updates that ledger's own decision, not this one.

serving_is_a_separate_ledger.rationale: This file's project is 'Model Creation Flow Refactor' and its global_definition_of_done is written entirely in terms of the five-step wizard and the Save Model persistence boundary. Serving is downstream of that boundary, has a different lifecycle (a long-running service, not a job that exits), a different failure model, and a different audience. Folding it in would move progress from 3/10 to 3/16 with no work regressing, and would leave MODEL-FLOW-008's end-to-end criterion looking incomplete for reasons unrelated to the flow it verifies. Same precedent this ledger already set twice: MODEL-FLOW-011 was kept out of MODEL-FLOW-002 for the same reason, and DS-LAKE put the DatasetDraft entity and its sweeper nine features apart.
serving_is_a_separate_ledger.coupling: Four hooks remain in THIS file and are added below: MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 (record what serving needs at adoption time), MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 (do not delete an adopted prefix), the note on MODEL-FLOW-005 that /retrain is the SAME undefined operation, and one new global_definition_of_done line. Everything else lives in MODEL-SERVE.

retrain_and_fine_tuning_are_one_question.note: A serving-plane POST /retrain and MODEL-FLOW-005's Fine-Tuning are not two features that happen to be similar — they are the same unanswered question wearing two names, and answering it once answers both. decisions.fine_tuning_undefined already states why: train.py fits once and exits, and HistGradientBoostingRegressor has no incremental warm start. Whatever /retrain turns out to mean (a fresh fit on a widened window, a hyperparameter search reusing the split, or a genuine warm start on a framework that supports one) is the same thing MODEL-FLOW-005 is blocked on. MODEL-SERVE-004 is therefore recorded as blocked on the identical decision rather than as independent work, so that resolving it cannot be double-counted.

serving_artifacts_stay_under_the_draft_p.note: MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 adopts run artifacts BY POINTER and never copies bytes, which is correct and matches DatasetArtifact. The consequence for serving, which nothing in this file states yet: the object a production model loads lives at drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/, permanently, under a prefix whose name says 'draft'. That is acceptable — renaming it would mean copying bytes, which the adoption rule exists to avoid — but it makes MODEL-FLOW-011-T02 (reclaim the runs' object prefixes) capable of deleting the bytes a live model is serving. See MODEL-FLOW-011-T05.

bucket_layout_is_downstream.note: MODEL-SERVE-007 separates object storage into buckets by retention class. TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS LEDGER, neither reopening a completed task. (1) MODEL-FLOW-003-T08's key shapes are UNCHANGED — every guard it built is key-structural and bucket-blind, confirmed by MODEL-FLOW-004's live execution of is_committed_artifact_key, so drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/ keeps its exact string in whichever bucket holds it. Nothing to redo. (2) MODEL-FLOW-011-T02's prefix reclaim will run against a bucket, so it must resolve the bucket rather than assume one; and once `models` is its own bucket, T05's run-level guard is additionally expressible as a bucket-scoped rule an operator can see — which is strictly better than a predicate only this repo knows about. Recorded here so whoever picks up 011 does not hardcode `datasets` into a sweep.

features.title: Unblock the Training Path — Correctness Prerequisites
features.description: Four defects that make the existing training path either impossible to start or unsafe to trust. None is a refactor; every one is a correctness fix that MODEL-FLOW-003 onward depend on. T02 in particular gates every metric Step 3 displays.
features.reaudit_note: Re-audited 2026-08-18 before implementation, by reading each named file directly (not by report). Five of the seven original tasks (T01, T03, T04, T05, T07) described code that was ALREADY CORRECT at commit 1df3c53 — the audit that produced this feature had drifted from the tree. T03's premise was inverted (memory 8 GiB > tmpfs 2 GiB, already consistent, not the reverse). Only T02 and T06 were live defects; both are now fixed. The likely cause of the drift: images/trainer/train.py:180-203 held a half-applied T02 patch (a broken orphan build_feature_spec with an undefined _reads_tag and an unimportable `spec = {...}` set-of-Ellipsis) — evidence someone started T02 before, landed the Pydantic field and helper functions, and left the wiring. See T08-T10 for defects found during re-audit that were NOT in the original task list.

tasks.title: Fix unsatisfiable artifact precondition in createRunService
tasks.detail: createRunService requires artifact.type === 'GOLD' AND artifact.datasetId != null. saveDraftAsDatasetService sets datasetId on the FINAL row only — a GOLD artifact keeps just its draftId — so no run can ever be created. Change to type === 'FINAL'. Nothing is lost: promoteDraftArtifactToFinalService copies objectKey/checksum/featureSpecKey from its source verbatim and writes no bytes, so FINAL and its GOLD parent are the same object with the same feature spec, and FINAL additionally carries the validationKey proving it passed the gate. Also restore the findUnique call, which was overwritten with a fragment of saveDraftAsDatasetService (references tx/finalArtifact/dataset, none in scope — the file does not compile).
tasks.verification_note: Re-verified 2026-08-18 by reading model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts directly: line 65 already reads `artifact.type !== 'FINAL'` (not 'GOLD'), the findUnique at line 61 is intact, and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors in this module. Already satisfied — no code change needed.

tasks.title: Record the target in feature_spec.json so the leakage guard can fire
tasks.detail: train.py::assert_no_target_leakage reads derived_from_target, target_y and target_scaled from feature_spec.json. build_feature_spec(features, selected_columns, scalers) has no target parameter and emits none of the three, so `derived` is always empty and the guard returns before checking anything. This is the highest-severity item in the plan: the failure it catches LOOKS LIKE SUCCESS. A lab target sampled daily against a 1-minute PI grid with any target-derived lag feature yields R² near 1.0, and Step 3 would render that with a convincing actual-vs-predicted chart. Requires threading the target through FeaturesRequest -> the NestJS DTO -> the client's Step 4 call, and computing derived_from_target from the feature configs. target_y/target_scaled/derived_from_target must NOT enter featureHash: they describe how a run READS the artifact, not how it was built, so two runs with different targets against the same bytes must still share a hash.
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18. build_feature_spec gained an optional 4th target_y param; when set it adds target_y/target_scaled/derived_from_target AFTER the hash is computed (never entering it). derived_from_target is a TRANSITIVE closure (a forward pass tracking every column that reads the target or an already-tainted column), not a direct-read check — the original task text under-specified this, and a direct-read predicate would miss a feature chained off an earlier target-derived feature. artifact_service.py::features() now also calls the existing (previously orphaned) force_keep_target helper once and reuses that same effective column list for both select_columns and build_feature_spec, so the spec never claims a different column set than what was actually written. Threaded through CreateFeaturesSchema (NestJS), both python call sites (inline /features route and the async job path incl. readFeatureRecipe), and the client (dwTargetTagAtom -> useDatasetGoldWarm -> startFeaturesJob), with targetTag added to the warming effect's dependency list. assert_target_is_unscaled was deliberately left uncalled — a scaled target is recorded truthfully and blocked later at training time by train.py's existing check, not at dataset-save time. Verified via 6 new pytest cases in test_feature_spec_quirks.py (14/14 pass) proving build_feature_spec's own contract, PLUS a 7th seam test (test_features_force_keeps_target_through_select_columns in test_artifact_service_features.py) proving the wiring at the call site actually works: with selected_columns deliberately omitting the target, both the WRITTEN BYTES and the spec's selectedColumns retain it — the first-pass draft of this note cited only the unit-level tests, which would have missed a broken call site. Full apps/python suite: 617 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (test_features_writes_feature_spec_sidecar_and_returns_its_key, confirmed via git stash to predate this branch), 66 skipped.

tasks.title: Fix container resource limits (tmpfs exceeds the memory cap)
tasks.detail: CORRECTED 2026-08-18: this task's premise was inverted against the tree. trainning-container.authorized.service.ts:27-29 sets Memory to 8 GiB (`8 * 1024 ** 3`) and line 92 sets the /scratch tmpfs to 2 GiB (`size=2g`) — memory already exceeds the tmpfs, which is the consistent direction, not the reverse this task described. Neither value is overridden by any TRAINING_MEMORY_BYTES/TRAINING_NANO_CPUS env var in .env or .env.example, so these code defaults are the effective, already-safe limits.
tasks.verification_note: Verified 2026-08-18 by reading trainning-container.authorized.service.ts:19-30,83-95 directly. Already satisfied — no code change needed. The residual risk the original reasoning still correctly names (tmpfs pages are charged to the container's memory cgroup, so /scratch + the in-memory DataFrame + sklearn all share the 8 GiB cap) remains true and worth monitoring under a large artifact, but is not a defect to fix.

tasks.title: Align the container's callback base path with the controller
tasks.detail: train.py builds API = {API_BASE}/internal/model/runs/{RUN_ID}; ModelRunAuthorizedController is @Controller('authorized/model/runs') behind the /api/v1 global prefix. Every callback 404s, starting with /claim. Pick one: either the container's path gains the real prefix, or the controller moves to internal/model/runs — the latter reads better, since 'authorized' means a user JWT everywhere else in this codebase and this controller explicitly does not take one.
tasks.verification_note: Verified 2026-08-18 by reading images/trainer/train.py:29-42 directly. Line 40 already builds `{API_BASE}/api/v1/authorized/model/runs/{RUN_ID}`, matching the controller's `authorized/model/runs` path behind `setGlobalPrefix('api')` + URI versioning v1. Already satisfied — no code change needed. Note: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile, so a deployed image tagged scgc/soft-sensor-trainer:1.0.0 could still carry stale train.py — the repo source is correct, deployment currency was not verified.

tasks.title: Stop leaking tokenHash from cancelRunService
tasks.detail: Its findFirst has no omit, and the early return for an already-terminal run returns that row straight to the caller. The other three read paths already omit it. A token hash reaching the browser is not exploitable on its own, but it is the kind of leak that becomes one after any change to how tokens are compared.
tasks.verification_note: Verified 2026-08-18 by reading model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:158-186 directly. `omit: { tokenHash: true }` is present on both the findFirst (line 167) and the update (line 177); the early-terminal-run return at line 170 returns the already-omitted row. Already satisfied — no code change needed.

tasks.title: Remove the debug print of the presign request
tasks.detail: routers/preprocess.py::presign_artifact prints the whole request body. Neither the request nor the response should reach a log: a presigned URL is a bearer capability for the artifact bytes, and anyone who can read the log can download them for the lifetime of the URL.
tasks.verification_note: Fixed 2026-08-18: deleted the `print(f"Presign request for artifact {body}")` at routers/preprocess.py:488-489. Confirmed this router module has no other importer besides main.py's route mount.

tasks.title: Delete the dead tag_stats path
tasks.detail: artifact_service.tag_stats duplicates column_stats line for line, references TagStatsRequest which is not imported (the module fails to import), and has no router endpoint. Its NestJS counterparts are equally broken: getDraftArtifactTagStatsService uses an unimported PythonTagStatsSchema, and getDraftArtifactStatsController calls a method name that does not exist. Remove all four, plus the POST /:id/artifacts/:artifactId/stats route.
tasks.verification_note: Verified 2026-08-18 via repo-wide grep for tag_stats|TagStatsRequest|PythonTagStatsSchema|getDraftArtifactTagStats|getDraftArtifactStatsController — zero hits anywhere in apps/backend, apps/python, or packages. Already satisfied — no code change needed.

tasks.title: Delete the orphan half-applied build_feature_spec in train.py
tasks.detail: Found during T02 re-audit, not in the original task list. images/trainer/train.py:180-203 held a second, broken copy of build_feature_spec: `spec = {...}` is a set containing Ellipsis (the next line's item assignment would raise TypeError), `_reads_tag` is undefined anywhere in the repo, and `feature_column_name` is not imported into train.py. Unreachable from main() — the trainer only ever reads feature_spec.json, it does not author one; the connector (feature_spec_service.py) owns that. Latent, not fatal, but the most plausible explanation for how T02 came to look already-attempted.
tasks.verification_note: Fixed 2026-08-18: deleted the orphan function. Confirmed via grep that nothing imports train.py as a module (it is a standalone container ENTRYPOINT).

tasks.title: Harden is_model_run_key against path traversal
tasks.detail: Found during re-audit. object_store.py's is_model_run_key was a substring test (`key.startswith('models/') and '/runs/' in key'`), so a malformed model_id like '../../x' would pass. Currently unreachable — the sole caller (presign_model_run_upload) builds keys only from run.modelId/run.id off the ModelTrainingRun row, never from a container-supplied id directly — but MODEL-FLOW-003-T08 widens this predicate to accept the draft scope too, which is when a malformed id becomes reachable.
tasks.verification_note: Fixed 2026-08-18: rewrote as a structural check requiring exactly 4 non-empty path segments after MODEL_ROOT (model_id/runs/run_id/filename), none of them '.' or '..', mirroring is_committed_artifact_key's sibling shape. Confirmed the sole caller (artifact_service.presign_model_run_upload) still passes with well-formed keys. Added test_is_model_run_key_rejects_traversal_and_malformed_segments to tests/test_object_store.py (8 cases: valid key, '../../x' traversal, mid-path '..', double-slash, extra segment, wrong literal, empty segment, wrong root) — all pass. This is the actual claim the task makes; a passing pre-existing suite alone would not have proven it.

tasks.title: Collapse the degenerate ternary in watch()
tasks.detail: Found during re-audit. trainning-container.authorized.service.ts:133 was `status: StatusCode === 0 ? 'FAILED' : 'FAILED'` — both branches identical, so the condition is dead code. The failureReason string two lines below correctly distinguishes a clean exit that never called /complete from a genuine crash; only the status assignment was affected.

features.title: Training Against a Draft, With No Model Commit
features.implementation: Backend done 2026-08-18 (T02/T04/T07/T08) — see each task's verification_note. Client done same day (T01/T03/T04/T05/T06/T09): use-model-training.ts rewritten — no longer calls useModelCommit(); instead validates (single target, single algorithm, algorithm in the training container's supported set, AutoML toggles off, dataset has a FINAL artifact), calls the new modelDraftRunService.create via authorized/model-drafts/:draftId/runs, and polls modelDraftRunService.get on a 2.5s interval until the run reaches a terminal status, resuming the poll on remount from ModelDraft.currentRunId if a run is still in flight. useModelDraftSync now exposes ensureDraftId so Start Training can guarantee a draft exists even if the 600ms PATCH debounce hasn't fired yet. TrainState gained lastLog (shown as text in place of the old fake progress bar — T09); mpTrainingResultAtom/mpArtifactRefAtom are populated from the completed run's metrics/modelKey on SUCCEEDED (T05/T06). T10 is the one open item, and its catalogue half was resolved 2026-08-19: validation now enforces exactly one target and one algorithm before a run is created; the wizard's algorithm catalogue (now 12 entries: ols/ridge/hist_gradient_boosting/svm/mlp/grp/pls/random_forest/lightgbm/xgboost/lstm/gru) is intentional per product decision, and train.py's build_model was extended to implement 10 of the 12 (images/trainer/train.py) — lstm/gru remain deferred to MODEL-FLOW-009 and disabled inline in the wizard. STILL OPEN: AutoML toggles (Find Best Model/Params) still have no training-container counterpart — that half of T10 stays blocked; see MODEL-FLOW-003-T10's blocked_reason for why it is not a build_model change.
features.description: Keep Step 2's experience unchanged while training runs against a ModelDraft. Training writes job rows (ModelTrainingRun, ModelTrainingRunLog) — it must, the container authenticates against one and reports into the other — but creates no Model. See decisions.persistence_boundary_clarified.

tasks.title: Keep existing Training button behavior
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18: Phase2TrainingConfig's button JSX (label/spinner/disabled logic driven by training.status) is untouched. The only visible change is what T09 asks for — the numeric progress bar is replaced by the latest log line while training. pnpm --filter=client check-types clean for this file.

tasks.title: Update training API to receive Model Draft context
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18: POST authorized/model-drafts/:draftId/runs (ModelDraftRunAuthorizedController -> createDraftRunService). Reuses buildRunData's artifact validation (FINAL type, checksum, datasetId, target-in-metadata, MIN_LABELLED_ROWS=30) unchanged from the Model-scoped path; refuses 400 if the draft is already SAVED or ABANDONED. pnpm --filter=backend check-types clean.

tasks.title: Remove persistent Model database commit from training
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18: use-model-training.ts no longer imports or calls useModelCommit(). Checked its only other caller (phase-4-deploy.tsx, Step 4's real Save Model path) and mpCreatedModelIdAtom's only other reader (use-model-pipeline-nav.ts's wizard-reset function) — neither is affected, so useModelCommit's create-once-then-update guard now takes its create branch correctly on the FIRST call, which is Step 4, not Step 2.

tasks.title: Run training against the Model Draft
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18: createDraftRunService runs an interactive $transaction creating the run (modelDraftId set, modelId null) then updating modelDraft.currentRunId, then mints a run token and spawns the container via the existing TrainningContainerAuthorizedService (untouched, already correct from MODEL-FLOW-000). Container reads its spec the same way regardless of owner. Client side (use-model-training.ts) now calls this via modelDraftRunService.create (services/model-draft.ts) after validating target/algorithm/dataset-artifact client-side — see the feature's own implementation note for what that guard covers.

tasks.title: Persist training result to temporary workspace
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18: DraftTrainingResult widened with runId + metrics (was algorithm/trainedAt only, a MODEL-FLOW-002 mock). use-model-training.ts's poll loop sets mpTrainingResultAtom on SUCCEEDED, passing run.metrics through as-is (Record<string, unknown> | null) — no Step 3 metric-key mapping attempted here, that belongs to the feature that wires Step 3 to real data. Nothing reads this atom yet (grep confirmed), so widening it broke no existing consumer.

tasks.title: Persist trained model artifact reference
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18: mpArtifactRefAtom set to run.modelKey on SUCCEEDED in the same poll-loop branch as T05 — the key already lives under drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/ per T08. Comment on the atom updated to drop the MODEL-FLOW-002 'mock, TODO' language since this is now real.

tasks.title: Update Model Draft state to TRAINED
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18: ModelDraftStatus enum gained TRAINED (migration 20260818085151_model_flow_003_draft_trained_status, applied live). ModelRunAuthorizedService.complete() resolves the run's owner and, for a draft-owned run going SUCCEEDED, runs an array-form $transaction updating the run AND modelDraft.status/currentRunId together — avoids a reader seeing a SUCCEEDED run against a still-ACTIVE draft. @softsensor/prisma needed its own `pnpm --filter=@softsensor/prisma build` (not just `prisma generate`) to refresh dist/ before the new enum value type-checked in the backend — prisma generate alone only refreshes src/generated/client, not the package's compiled output its package.json types/main point at. pnpm --filter=backend check-types now clean (only the 4 pre-existing unrelated auth/**/*.spec.ts errors remain, confirmed via git diff --stat against those files showing no changes this session).

tasks.title: Scope run outputs under the draft prefix
tasks.detail: presign_model_run_upload writes to models/{modelId}/runs/{runId}/, but no modelId exists when the container uploads. Move to drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/ and widen is_model_run_key/model_run_key accordingly — that predicate is the only thing standing between a malformed id and a write outside the models prefix, so widening it needs its own test.
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18: DRAFT_ROOT/draftRunPrefix/draftRunKey added in artifact-keys.ts and object_store.py (kept as separate functions from the model versions, not merged, to keep each root's structural check independent). is_draft_run_key added with the same 4-segment/no-traversal validation as is_model_run_key. ModelRunUploadPresignRequest widened with an exactly_one_owner model_validator (mirrors MaterializeRequest.exactly_one_source's existing pattern); presign_model_run_upload branches on draft_id vs model_id. presignModelRunUpload's TS signature changed to a discriminated union enforcing exactly-one-of at compile time. ModelRunAuthorizedService.mintUploadUrls/complete both resolve owner first and branch the key builder accordingly. Verified: apps/python/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_object_store.py -k run_key -q -> 4 passed. Full python suite also run: 595 passed, 66 skipped, 1 failed — the failure (test_features_writes_feature_spec_sidecar_and_returns_its_key, a column_stats_key assertion) is unrelated and pre-existing, confirmed absent from this session's diff of both artifact_service.py and its test file.

tasks.title: Replace the mock progress ramp with real polling
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18: the 400ms x6 setInterval ramp is gone. On create, use-model-training.ts polls modelDraftRunService.get(draftId, runId) (wraps GET authorized/model-drafts/:draftId/runs/:runId, which includes logs like getRunService does) every 2.5s until the run reaches SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELED. Progress stays a plain number (0 while training, 100 on done) so RuntimeEstimate's existing ETA math (progress > 5 gate) degrades safely without needing changes to that file; the actual INDETERMINATE signal is TrainState.lastLog, rendered as text in Phase2TrainingConfig in place of the old <Progress> bar (components/ui/progress.tsx is shadcn-generated/immutable and has no indeterminate styling to lean on). A mount effect resumes polling from ModelDraft.currentRunId if trainState.status is still 'training' after a remount. Hardened after review: a single dropped poll no longer surfaces as an error — a transient failure would otherwise push the user to Retrain, which spawns a SECOND container against the same draft (the backend only refuses a SAVED/ABANDONED draft, not a still-training one). failCountRef tolerates up to MAX_CONSECUTIVE_POLL_FAILURES (3) misses in a row, reset on any success, before giving up.

tasks.title: Narrow Step 2 to one target and one algorithm
tasks.detail: train.py fits spec['targetY'], a single string, and one algorithm. Today's multi-select would silently train on whichever entry sorted first. Also: the UI's split is a percentage while chronological_split multiplies by the row count — 80 instead of 0.8 slices at 80x the length and raises 'leaves one side empty' with a number nobody can trace to a slider. Convert once, at the client boundary, and have the API refuse anything outside (0.5, 0.95).
tasks.verification_note: Split-ratio conversion was already done (useModelDraftSync's PATCH, MODEL-FLOW-002) and the API-side clamp was already done (CreateTrainingRunSchema.trainTestSplit min(0.5).max(0.95)) — both pre-date this task. 2026-08-18: use-model-training.ts refuses to create a run unless targetVariables.length === 1 and algorithms.length === 1, so a multi-select can no longer silently train on whichever entry sorted first — it errors instead, visibly. 2026-08-19: the catalogue half of blocked_reason is resolved — see below. Task stays blocked on the AutoML half only.
tasks.blocked_reason: CATALOGUE HALF RESOLVED 2026-08-19: product decision made — the wizard's Algorithm catalogue (12 entries: ols/ridge/hist_gradient_boosting/svm/mlp/grp/pls/random_forest/lightgbm/xgboost/lstm/gru) is intentional; every algorithm is meant to run against real plant data and be compared before anything is narrowed. train.py's build_model was extended to cover 10 of the 12 (images/trainer/train.py); the bare 'hgb' string was dropped from the client-facing enum (kept as a build_model branch alongside 'hist_gradient_boosting' for backend compatibility only — one algorithm, one client-facing id); lstm/gru are deferred to MODEL-FLOW-009 (a data-shape/pipeline change, not a build_model branch) and disabled inline in AlgorithmSelector with a stated reason so a user cannot select a run that will always fail. STILL BLOCKED — AUTOML HALF: Find Best Model / Find Best Params have no training-container counterpart, and this task does not resolve that — one run fits one algorithm; AutoML is N runs orchestrated ABOVE the container (a client/backend loop calling create-run repeatedly and comparing results), not a flag passed into train.py. Sizing that as a build_model change would understate it the same way sizing lstm/gru as one would have. T10's client-side AutoML refusal (use-model-training.ts, "AutoML ... isn't wired to a real training run yet") stays in place unchanged. Decision needed before this task can close: define the AutoML orchestration loop, or formally drop the two toggles from the UI.

Clicking Training starts a real container.
Training creates NO Model row. It does create ModelTrainingRun and ModelTrainingRunLog rows — required for the container to authenticate and report.
The run references a ModelDraft, not a Model.
Training metrics are available to Step 3 Evaluation.
Run artifacts are written under the draft's own object prefix.
Training completion sets the draft state to TRAINED.

verification.description: Run training from Step 2 and verify SELECT count(*) FROM "Model" is unchanged, while a ModelTrainingRun row exists against the draft.
verification.note: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-19 against the real dev stack (Postgres, MinIO, nest --watch backend, real browser session). Envelope bug (see prior note in history) found and fixed same session: createDraftRunService/getDraftRunService/listDraftRunsService/cancelDraftRunService now return {statusCode,message,type,data} matching ModelDraftAuthorizedService's convention; client's created.data.id / res.data no longer read off undefined. Confirmed with two real runs against real plant data (draft 38048766-dd15-4e1d-9c5d-8969f1cf11fb, artifact S204FBP.lab target, algorithms ols and svm) both reaching ModelTrainingRun.status=SUCCEEDED with real metrics, 4 uploaded artifact keys each, and ModelDraft.status transitioning to TRAINED with currentRunId pointing at the latest run. `Model` table has 17 pre-existing rows unrelated to these runs; createDraftRunService's transaction has zero prisma.model.create/update calls (confirmed by direct code read, not just row-count diff) — the DB-level guarantee this criterion asks for. One orphaned run (562ec955, svm, stuck RUNNING, zero log lines, container since removed) was also observed — traced to a nest --watch hot-reload restart killing the in-memory watch() tracker mid-flight while this session was actively editing the backend file being verified; the container itself is independent of the Node process and either failed silently before its first log line or was removed outside watch()'s own reap() path. This is a pre-existing gap in watch()'s design (no reconciliation of orphaned RUNNING rows on backend boot) — not a defect in the envelope fix, and out of scope to fix here; noted for whoever picks up resilience work on the container-watch path.

features.title: Preserve Evaluation Flow Using Model Draft Results
features.description: Keep the existing Step 5 Evaluation UI (renumbering history: MODEL-FLOW-010 moved this to Step 4 on 2026-08-20; MODEL-FLOW-013 inserted Model Selection at Step 4 on 2026-08-27, shifting this entry to Step 5 — this description named 'Step 3' before MODEL-FLOW-010's own pass) and ensure that evaluation metrics and charts use the Model Draft's real training run instead of requiring a persisted Model database record.
features.implementation:
Done 2026-08-25. AUDITED FIRST, per CLAUDE.md §18: this entry was one of the thin, never-re-audited ones (5 bare task titles, no detail) — read against the tree before scoping, not against the prior task titles. FINDING: Phase3Evaluation was not 'using a stale API', it used NO real data source at all — it re-materialised the dataset client-side and fit a 2-variable OLS line over the target plus 'the first non-target tag it finds' (`computeFit`, old `lib/model-metrics.ts:150`), ignoring the trained algorithm entirely. The run's real output was already captured on SUCCEEDED (MODEL-FLOW-003-T05/T06) into `mpTrainingResultAtom`/`mpArtifactRefAtom` and READ BY NOTHING — confirmed by grep, zero readers of either atom before this pass.

No read path for a run's predictions existed anywhere in the stack — confirmed by executing the guard live: `is_committed_artifact_key('drafts/{d}/runs/{r}/predictions.parquet')` returns False, and the four existing parse endpoints (`/rows`, `/preview`, `/histogram`, `/scatter`) all route through `sample_rows`, which assumes per-tag `__status` sidecar columns a run's 3-column `{timestamp, y_true, y_pred}` frame does not have. Built new: `POST /v1/preprocess/models/runs/predictions` (`artifact_service.run_predictions`) — reads the full test-split frame, computes `row_count`/`residual_sd`/a `residual_rmse_check` cross-check/y-ranges over the FULL frame (no decimation branch: `MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS=20000`, comfortably above the largest observed run at 4,633 rows; a run over the cap is refused by name rather than silently sampled — deferred design recorded in `schemas/preprocess.py`'s own comment for whoever hits it first), and optionally reads `run_manifest.json` for `derived_from_target`/`target_scaled`. `GET .../model-drafts/:draftId/runs/:runId/predictions` (`getDraftRunPredictionsService`) resolves `predictionsKey`/`manifestKey` OFF THE RUN ROW, never from the request — same discipline `mintUploadUrls` already applies on the write side — and refuses (404, naming which) a run that has not SUCCEEDED or has no `predictionsKey`. Client: `modelDraftRunService.predictions` + new `useDraftRunEvaluation` hook, keyed on `(draftId, runId)` with a fallback to `ModelDraft.currentRunId` when the atom hint is empty (mirrors `use-model-training.ts`'s own reconnect-effect trust in that field). `lib/model-metrics.ts` rewritten: `computeFit`/`computeMetrics`/`pickDefaultPair` DELETED (grepped: Step 4 was `computeFit`'s only caller; the other two already had zero callers, confirmed dead before removal), replaced by `fitFromRun(points, {r2,rmse,sd})` — a pure wrap, no fitting. `phase-3-evaluation.tsx` rewritten around the hook; kept `METRIC_KEY`/`METRIC_META`/`buildFitRows`/both chart components/the histogram+Q-Q section entirely unchanged, per the seam the old module's own doc comment specified.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO A PRIOR READING, RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENTLY FIXED (MinIO screenshot findings in MODEL-FLOW-010/MODEL-SERVE-000 called `holdoutMetrics` null on every observed run and left the cause open): (1) confirmed via the one real log line that exists (`Holdout replay skipped: Could not read '.../validate_data.parquet': NoSuchKey`) — it fails at the REPLAY step on a missing source object, not at presign. `train.py`'s own comment already documents this as the common case (no holdout on the dataset), not a bug. (2) There IS a real, separate, still-latent defect one line later: `tryReplayHoldout`'s own `presignArtifact({source_key: targetKey})` call presigns `.../validate_ready.parquet`, which the SAME committed-artifact guard refuses (verified by executing it: `is_committed_artifact_key` returns False for that key too) — it has simply never been reached by any observed run. Recorded against DS-LAKE-018-T05, not fixed here — it is not this ledger's to fix, and 'holdoutMetrics is null' already has its real, boring cause.

SCOPE DECISIONS (user-confirmed, not unilateral): (a) the 'Compare with…' control is DISABLED with a stated reason, not removed and not left fabricating a series — `seededNoise`/`comparePoints`/`compareFit` deleted; no saved Model can supply a real predicted series until MODEL-FLOW-007 adopts a run by pointer, so faking one here would be the same defect this feature exists to remove. (b) Resuming a TRAINED draft into Step 4 (MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's recorded gap 1) stays OUT of scope — `useDraftRunEvaluation`'s `(draftId, runId)` key with the `currentRunId` fallback is deliberately shaped so that resume work is a follow-on, not a rewrite, when someone picks it up. (c) Metric cards stay exactly r2/rmse/sd — MAE rides in the served payload, undisplayed, rather than widening `MetricKey` against acceptance criterion 1.

HONEST EMPTY STATES ADDED — the one place criterion 1 ('UI remains unchanged') had to bend, stated rather than discovered: no run yet, run still training, run FAILED/CANCELED (names the reason), and the load/error states from the hook itself. Load-bearing among these: `use-model-wizard-mode.ts:169-170` force-unlocks all 5 steps and sets `trainState:'done'` on EDIT MODE purely because the dataset resolved — there is no run, no `runId`, and `useModelCommit` persists neither on Save. Step 4 in edit mode therefore always hits the no-run empty state until MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 records a run reference on the saved Model.

Renamed 'Validation residual diagnostics' -> 'Test-split residual diagnostics': `predictions.parquet` is the run's TEST split, not the validation holdout, which is a distinct object with its own (currently always-null, see above) metrics shown on Step 2's own Holdout panel — the old heading misnamed what the histogram/Q-Q actually summarise.

features.title: Implement Background Fine-Tuning Process
features.description: Add an asynchronous background fine-tuning process that operates on the trained Model Draft and does not commit the model to the database.
features.unblocked: 2026-08-25, user decision: fine-tuning = a HYPERPARAMETER SEARCH over one algorithm/artifact/split, N hyperparameter sets tried in sequence, best kept by RMSE. Recorded in decisions.fine_tuning_undefined (this file) — MODEL-SERVE's decisions.retrain_and_fine_tuning_are_one_question names the same question for /retrain; that ledger still needs its own note updated when someone picks up MODEL-SERVE-004, not duplicated here.
features.implementation:
Built 2026-08-25, backend only — no client wiring in this pass (not asked for; the wizard's existing AutoML/Find-Best-Params toggles stay disabled, MODEL-FLOW-003-T10's own note still applies). No new spawn/claim/complete/queue infrastructure: a fine-tuning job is a ModelFineTuningJob row that GROUPS ordinary ModelTrainingRun rows (new nullable fineTuningJobId FK), each one launched through the EXACT MODEL-FLOW-003 machinery, live-verified end to end. This is the direct build-out of MODEL-FLOW-003-T10's own blocked_reason: 'AutoML is N runs orchestrated ABOVE the container ... not a flag passed into train.py.'

Extraction, not duplication: `ModelRunLaunchAuthorizedService.createDraftRunService` was split into `assertDraftWritable` (access+lifecycle gate, now public) + `launchDraftRun` (the actual write, now takes an optional `fineTuningJobId`, no user/role param). `createDraftRunService` itself is unchanged in behaviour — it calls both in sequence — verified by its own pre-existing 7-test suite passing unmodified. `launchDraftRun` is what both the job's first run (`ModelFineTuningAuthorizedService.createJob`) and every chained run (`advanceJobForRun`) call — a fine-tuning child run goes through the SAME buildRunData validation, the SAME transaction shape, the SAME trackSpawn fire-and-forget spawn as a normal single run.

Advancing a job (`advanceJobForRun`) is IDEMPOTENT, keyed by a compare-and-swap `updateMany` WHERE `(id, currentRunId, status IN (QUEUED,RUNNING))` — calling it twice for the same terminated run is a no-op the second time, unit-tested directly. Two call sites, both wired: `ModelRunAuthorizedService.complete()` calls it as a best-effort nudge (wrapped so it can NEVER fail the container's webhook response — a training container has no way to retry a 500), and `getJobService` calls it opportunistically on every read, so a job whose nudge was lost (the exact class of gap MODEL-FLOW-011-T04 already tracks for a single orphaned run) still advances the next time anyone looks at it. No cron, no queue, no BullMQ/Redis — CLAUDE.md §11's instruction to reuse or justify before introducing one.

REAL BUG CAUGHT WHILE WIRING, not by review: `complete()`'s existing SUCCEEDED-draft branch unconditionally set `ModelDraft.currentRunId = runId` — correct for a normal run, WRONG for a fine-tuning child run finishing mid-search, which would have pointed the draft at whichever INTERMEDIATE hyperparameter set happened to finish, not the eventual winner (and MODEL-FLOW-004's `useDraftRunEvaluation` would have shown that intermediate run in Step 4 for the whole search's duration). Fixed by excluding `!!run.fineTuningJobId` from that branch — only `advanceJobForRun`'s own completion branch may now set `ModelDraft.currentRunId`, and only to the true best run. Live-verified this fix works: `bestRunId` was correctly `86728c46...` (rmse 0.659) not `f8c1c1e0...` (the run that finished LAST, rmse 0.677, worse) — see V01's note.

Selection metric is RMSE, minimized, not configurable — R² was explicitly rejected: a real observed run scored r2 = -1,110,858 (MODEL-FLOW-004's own finding) while rmse stayed a sane, comparable number. Concurrency: a partial unique index (`ModelFineTuningJob_one_live_per_draft`, hand-added to the migration same precedent as 20260818021900_model_flow_002_owner_check) refuses a second QUEUED/RUNNING job per draft at the database — live-verified with a real concurrent-POST 409, not just a service-level check.

No BullMQ/Redis/Celery introduced, per CLAUDE.md §11 — training already has no such infrastructure to reuse, and the reconcile-on-read design (see implementation note) makes a real queue's core value (surviving a crash) unnecessary to build separately.

tasks.title: Update Fine-Tuning job status
tasks.verification_note: QUEUED -> RUNNING -> SUCCEEDED|FAILED, mirroring ModelRunStatus's own vocabulary (SUCCEEDED/CANCELED, not COMPLETED/CANCELLED — this ledger's job_states line below was itself stale against that convention and is corrected here) rather than inventing a parallel one, the same discipline MODEL-SERVE-003-T01's own note states for a different job type. `GET .../fine-tuning/:jobId` reconciles before returning live status.

tasks.title: Support Fine-Tuning failure handling
tasks.verification_note: MVP semantics, stated not hidden: any child run FAILED or CANCELED fails the WHOLE job — no partial-tolerance mode (skip this set, keep going). failureReason names which hyperparameter set (Nth of totalRuns) and why. A launch failure mid-chain (e.g. the draft was abandoned between sets) is caught and also fails the job, never left stranded RUNNING with a dead currentRunId.

tasks.title: Support Fine-Tuning retry
tasks.verification_note: Only a FAILED job retries, relaunching the EXACT hyperparameter set that failed (`completedRuns` deliberately not incremented on failure, so `sets[completedRuns]` is always that set) and resuming the sequence from there. Live-verified against a real (deliberately-triggered) FAILED job: relaunch succeeded, job returned to RUNNING with a fresh currentRunId. NOT covered, stated explicitly: a job stuck RUNNING because its current run is itself orphaned (a nest --watch restart killing the in-memory container tracker mid-flight, MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's own observed incident) — retry only fires on FAILED; that gap is MODEL-FLOW-011-T04's, not duplicated here.

features.title: Persist Model Configuration and Artifacts Before Final Save
features.description: Store model configuration, training configuration, evaluation results, and model artifacts in temporary or external storage while keeping the final Model database record uncommitted.
features.implementation:
AUDITED FIRST 2026-08-25, per CLAUDE.md §18 — another thin, never-re-audited entry (6 bare task titles). FIVE OF SIX TASKS WERE ALREADY SATISFIED by work already landed: training config lives on ModelDraft (8 PATCHable fields) + the authoritative reproducible spec on ModelTrainingRun (checksum, imageDigest, featureSpecKey, seed, computed cut_timestamp — strictly more than the draft holds); fine-tuning config on ModelFineTuningJob (built in -005, same session); evaluation on ModelTrainingRun.metrics/.holdoutMetrics (read path built in -004); artifact references are the run's own modelKey/metricsKey/manifestKey/predictionsKey; 'latest valid' is ModelDraft.currentRunId (+ ModelFineTuningJob.bestRunId). This is architecturally the SAME shape the ledger's own precedent already uses for datasets: DatasetDraft holds identity + currentArtifactId, the recipe lives on DatasetArtifact.operations — ModelDraft holds identity + currentRunId, the spec lives on the run row.

THE ONE REAL DEFECT, found by querying the live dev DB rather than reading code alone: `ModelConfigSchema` (model.authorized.dto.ts) was `.passthrough()` and declared only 6 of the ~18 keys the client actually sends, with its own comment stating 'the canonical shape lives in the client type; the backend only stores it round-trip.' A live audit of all 16 existing Model rows found the drift that allowed: 6 dead pre-Data-Studio ETL keys (dataSource, fillStrategies, timeRange, selectedTags, customDateRange, savedSourceId) persisted verbatim, and BOTH targetVariable (declared, singular) and targetVariables (used, undeclared, plural) present across rows — the field real data mostly uses survived only because nothing validated it. Also found: trainTestSplit is a PERCENTAGE in Model.data.config (70/80/85 observed) but a FRACTION on ModelDraft.splitRatio and ModelTrainingRun.splitSpec.ratio — three homes, two units, unvalidated on the one that matters here.

FIXED: ModelConfigSchema rewritten from .passthrough() to .strict(), declaring every field actually seen in production — live fields typed properly (targetVariables[], algorithms[], findBestModel/findBestParams, lossFunction, deployment, etc.), the 6 dead ETL keys and the singular targetVariable kept as explicitly @deprecated z.unknown()/string fields so legacy rows keep validating. trainTestSplit validated as a percentage (.min(50).max(95)) with a comment naming all three homes and their units — unifying the unit is -007's job, when Save Model can derive it from the adopted run's own splitSpec instead of trusting the browser. New DeploymentConfigSchema declared (autoRetrain/warnSd/criticalSd/driftMonitor/driftThresholdPct) even though 0 of 16 rows carry it and no UI currently writes it (phase-4-deploy.tsx's own docblock says so) — -007 decides whether to wire the UI or delete the field and its 5 client atoms, not decided here.

THE TRAP THIS DESIGN HAD TO AVOID, LIVE-VERIFIED CLOSED: updateModelService replaces config WHOLESALE, not by merge, and edit mode loads an existing Model's config then sends it back on save — a naively strict schema would have broken every edit of the 16 legacy rows. Verified against a REAL legacy row (5848c20f-..., carrying all 6 dead ETL keys) through the RUNNING backend: PATCH with its own config re-sent returned 200, and a direct DB equality check (`data->'config' = <original>::jsonb`) confirmed the stored blob is byte-identical, not merely 'still valid'. The refusal half was verified the same way: PATCHing an unknown key against the same live row returned 400 naming the exact key.

Also tightened: PatchModelDraftSchema.hyperparameters (model-draft.authorized.dto.ts) went from z.unknown() to the same HyperparametersSchema scalar constraint the run path already enforces — a draft could otherwise hold a hyperparameter value CreateTrainingRunSchema would refuse at Start Training, discovered only then. Confirmed compatible with the client's own HyperparamValue type (string|number|boolean|null) before tightening.

STILL RECORDED, NOT FIXED HERE (handed to -007, which is where they actually belong): 0 of 18 training runs have ever had modelId set; 0 of 24 drafts have ever had savedModelId set — the draft-to-Model bridge has never been exercised, confirming -007-T11's own 'UNVERIFIED PREMISE' framing was right to doubt itself. Save Model's commit payload (use-model-commit.ts:56-68) sends no runId/modelKey/metrics at all — this is why a saved Model today cannot be traced to what produced it, and it is exactly what -007-T10's adopt-by-pointer is for. Also recorded for whoever next touches these areas: two dead client inconsistencies (lossFunction default disagrees between resetWizardAtom 'mse' and resetPipeline 'rmse'; resetPipeline hardcodes the metric array instead of importing METRIC_KEYS), ~29 dead client atoms/hooks from the pre-Data-Studio wizard, and CreateModelRunSchema (model-run.authorized.dto.ts) confirmed dead code via grep with a harmless bound mismatch against the live schema.

New DeploymentConfigSchema added, currently unused by any row. LIVE-VERIFIED against a real legacy row through the running backend: PATCH re-sending its own config -> 200, DB-level byte-identical; PATCH with an unknown key -> 400 naming it. 9/9 new unit tests (model.authorized.dto.spec.ts) including the byte-for-byte legacy round-trip fixture pulled from the real DB.

features.title: Commit Model Only on Step 4 Save Model
features.description: Keep the existing Step 4 Save Model UI but make it the only persistence boundary where the Model Draft becomes a persistent Model record.
features.implementation:
Built and LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-31 (fifth pass, continuing MODEL-FLOW-011's session). One new route owns the whole commit: POST authorized/model-drafts/:id/save (saveDraftService, model-draft.authorized.service.ts), mirroring saveDraftAsDatasetService's shape — assertDraftAccess, 409-on-SAVED, resolveActiveRunId (reused as-is, MODEL-FLOW-013-T08's resolver, no change needed), 422-no-run/422-not-SUCCEEDED/422-no-modelKey, a name-collision pre-check mirroring createModelService's own, a node-workspace check ALSO mirroring createModelService's own (added mid-pass, see findings), a best-effort manifest read for T11, then one $transaction: model.create + modelTrainingRun.update({modelId}) + modelDraft.update({status:'SAVED', savedModelId}). createModelService/updateModelService are UNTOUCHED — they stay the general-purpose model-registration endpoints use-model-form.ts's separate quick-add dialog still needs.

Config is DERIVED SERVER-SIDE from the adopted run via ModelConfigSchema.parse(), not trusted from the client — algorithm/algorithms/targetVariables/hyperparameters come off the run row, trainTestSplit is Math.round(run.splitSpec.ratio * 100) (the exact fraction-to-percentage fix ModelConfigSchema's own comment names as this feature's job). The client POST body shrank to what a user can still choose at Save time: name/nodeId/description/deployment (new SaveModelDraftSchema). use-model-commit.ts's create-mode branch now calls modelDraftService.save(draftId, ...) instead of createModel(...); its edit-mode branch (an already-saved Model's Save Changes) is UNCHANGED, per plan. phase-6-deploy.tsx needed one small fix beyond the wiring: its handleSave catch was swallowing every error into one generic 'Failed to save' string, including a 409-already-saved that isn't retryable — now surfaces err.message from the ApiError the fetcher already throws.

T10 (adopt by pointer): ModelTrainingRun.modelId is set, object keys stay under drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/... forever — the same DatasetArtifact-pointer premise, EXCEPT the identical dataset-side decision was later reversed by DS-LAKE-025 (copies bytes) because a cleanup sweep could reclaim draft-space bytes out from under it. User explicitly chose to stay pointer-only here (AskUserQuestion, this pass), relying on MODEL-FLOW-011-T05's adopted-run sweeper guard (built same session, one pass earlier) to make it safe — this Save is the first real exercise of that guard against a genuinely adopted row.

T06/T07 (artifact + metrics 'associated with' the saved Model): no new Prisma column on Model. Model.modelTrainingRuns (relation, already declared) + the now-populated ModelTrainingRun.modelId gives a saved Model's artifact keys/checksum/metrics/holdoutMetrics for free via the existing relation — reading model.modelTrainingRuns[0], which is exactly one run per draft in this pass (a second Save is refused at the 409 check).

T11 (framework_versions): images/trainer/train.py gained a module-level `import sklearn` and a framework_versions dict (sklearn always; lightgbm/xgboost only when that algorithm trained) written into run_manifest.json. New Python endpoint POST /v1/preprocess/models/runs/manifest (get_run_manifest, mirrors get_run_loss_history's structural-guard shape exactly) reads just that one field — every other manifest field already has a column on ModelTrainingRun, so nothing else was duplicated. New backend wrapper getRunManifest (python-preprocess-client.ts). Declared NULLABLE everywhere (Python response, Zod schema, ModelConfigSchema.frameworkVersions) — a legacy pre-1.0.3 manifest has no such key, and Save must not 422 an otherwise-valid old run over a field that predates it. TRAINING_IMAGE default bumped 1.0.2 -> 1.0.3 (trainning-container.authorized.service.ts) — user chose to actually `docker build` it this pass rather than leave the default pointing at an image that doesn't exist locally; confirmed via the running backend's own boot log ('Training image pinned to scgc/soft-sensor-trainer@sha256:29ed89...'), digest matches the build output exactly.

A CRITICAL PLACEMENT DECISION, caught by design review before writing any code, not found afterward: `frameworkVersions` was first drafted as a SIBLING key on Model.data (alongside config), which model.authorized.service.ts's normalizeData() would have silently stripped on the very next updateModel call — Save & Deploy's OWN immediate deployStatus:'running' follow-up write. Moved inside `config` (which normalizeData DOES whitelist) and declared as a new optional field on ModelConfigSchema itself. Verified this actually survives by reading updateModelService directly (model.authorized.service.ts:216-243): it merges from `normalizeData(existing.data)`, not from the DTO, so an update that omits `config` leaves the existing row's config — including frameworkVersions — untouched. This is also why the plan's original `data.savedFrom` idea was dropped rather than built: redundant with ModelTrainingRun.modelId + ModelDraft.savedModelId, which already encode both directions of the link, so there was nothing worth risking the same trap for.

LIVE-VERIFIED end to end against real dev-environment data (see verification block below for exact ids/evidence) — including a real divergence between the draft's stale client-side config (algorithm 'ols') and the adopted run's actual algorithm ('hist_gradient_boosting'), which is exactly the bug this feature exists to close, proven with a real saved row rather than a synthetic fixture.

features.title: Sequence Model Training (LSTM/GRU) — Deferred, Needs a Windowing Pipeline
features.description: The wizard's Algorithm catalogue includes lstm and gru; train.py's build_model raises a named error for both rather than the generic 'Unsupported algorithm' message, and the wizard disables both inline (AlgorithmSelector) so a user cannot select a run that will always fail. This feature is what it would take to actually run them — not scoped or estimated as part of the 10-algorithm tabular extension, because the shape of the work is different in kind, not degree.
features.implementation:
T01-T03 built and unit-verified 2026-08-31 (pure pandas/numpy, no image rebuild, no torch — user-confirmed scope for this pass). Three new functions in images/trainer/train.py, inserted directly after chronological_split: build_windows (2D frame -> (n_windows, sequence_length, n_features) X plus paired y/target_timestamps), chronological_split_windows (chronological_split's own cut-index rule, applied to window count instead of row count), and assert_no_window_leakage (the T02 guard). DEFAULT_SEQUENCE_LENGTH=24 added as a module constant. Deliberately NOT wired into main(): build_model's lstm/gru branch still raises before any of this would run, and the API/enum already refuses lstm/gru before a container is ever spawned — so main()'s live 10-algorithm flow (used by every real training run today) is untouched by this addition, and wiring dead code into it was judged unnecessary risk for zero live benefit this pass. T04 is where a real caller starts invoking these.

Two design corrections made explicit rather than guessed past (both via advisor review before coding): (1) T01's original framing implied windowing over the labelled (post-filter) frame — that is a real bug, not a simplification: consecutive rows in `labelled` are not consecutive in wall-clock time (module docstring's own daily-lab-target-over-1-minute-grid example), so windowing over it would silently span days instead of grid-steps, and assert_no_target_leakage would not catch it (returns early when `derived` is empty). build_windows instead windows the FULL time-ordered frame and gates only a window's INCLUSION on its target row's label_mask — proven by test_build_windows_spans_true_grid_spacing_not_labelled_only_spacing, which constructs the exact splice a labelled-only implementation would produce and asserts against it. (2) T02 is one assertion, not new analysis: a window keyed on its target row cannot straddle the cut by construction (span [i-sequence_length+1, i] is always entirely pre-cut for a correctly train-assigned window) — the real failure mode is assigning windows by START index instead of TARGET index, which assert_no_window_leakage catches (test_assert_no_window_leakage_catches_start_indexed_assignment_bug simulates exactly that bug). Windowing convention is NOWCAST (window predicts the target at its own last timestep), not forecast — matches every other algorithm's same-timestamp convention and keeps predictions.parquet's schema unchanged; no forecast/lookback-window concept exists anywhere else in this codebase to anchor the alternative (confirmed empty grep for horizon/forecast_ahead/n_steps_ahead).

T03: apps/client/lib/training-config.ts's HYPERPARAMS.lstm/.gru each gained a sequence_length number field (default 24, min 1, matching DEFAULT_SEQUENCE_LENGTH). Three vitest files consume HYPERPARAMS transitively (grep-confirmed importers) and all three were run, not just the one edited: lib/__tests__/training-config.test.ts (its pinned key-set assertion updated to include sequence_length, 15/15 pass), lib/run-params.test.ts and hooks/model/__tests__/use-apply-run-params.test.tsx (the run-parameter-recall path — unedited, 26/26 pass, confirming the added key does not break round-tripping). The DTO half needed NO change, confirmed by reading it fresh this pass rather than assumed: HyperparametersSchema (apps/backend/.../model-run.authorized.dto.ts) is already `z.record(z.string(), z.union([string,number,boolean,null]))` — a generic scalar record that accepts sequence_length today with no schema edit, so this task is genuinely smaller than its own original framing implied.

V01/V02: attempted live re-verification, not just source reading — started the backend standalone (pnpm --filter backend dev) to mint a token and POST a real run with algorithm:'lstm', but it failed to boot (`JwtStrategy requires a secret or key`). Root cause VERIFIED, not left as a guess: JWT_ACCESS_SECRET IS present in the root .env (confirmed via grep), but app.module.ts:31's `ConfigModule.forRoot({isGlobal:true})` passes no envFilePath, so it defaults to `.env` relative to `process.cwd()` — and `pnpm --filter backend dev` runs with cwd apps/backend, which has no `.env` of its own, so the root file is never read. An environment-loading gap unrelated to this feature (out of scope, not fixed here). Left PENDING, not completed, per CLAUDE.md 16 (an unperformed action must not read as done) — they join the existing browser/live-session-gated pile (-010-V01/V03/V04/V05, -013-V04/V05/V06, -004-V02/V03) rather than being marked verified on source-reading alone. Source reads (unchanged this pass, kept as each item's note) still say both hold: algorithm-selector.tsx:30-31 disables both with 'Needs sequence support not yet in the trainer' (V01), and CreateModelRunSchema.algorithm: TrainingAlgorithmEnum is enforced by the app-wide ZodValidationPipe (APP_PIPE, app.module.ts:75) (V02) — MODEL-FLOW-008's prior LIVE run exercised this same enum/pipe wiring end to end, just not for lstm/gru specifically.

Test-environment caveat, worth recording per this feature's own MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 lesson (a version mismatch between write and read LOOKS LIKE SUCCESS): the 21 test_train.py passes ran under an UNPINNED scratch venv (numpy/pandas/scikit-learn latest), not images/trainer/requirements.txt's pins (numpy==2.1.3, pandas==2.2.3) — the pinned numpy had no prebuilt wheel for the base system python available this pass. T04's image build is the first time this new code runs on the real pins.

=== T04, 2026-08-31 (same session, second pass) === Full T04 built and LIVE-VERIFIED end to end, closing the caveat above — the test-environment gap it named is now moot, since T04's own verification runs test_train.py inside the REAL built image on the REAL pins, not a scratch venv. torch==2.5.1 (CPU-only wheel, --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu in requirements.txt) resolved cleanly for this host's linux/aarch64 cp312 target — the pin-by-hope fallback design decision was never needed. New images/trainer/sequence_model.py: SequenceRegressor, a sklearn-shaped (.fit/.predict) wrapper around a single-layer LSTM/GRU -> last-hidden-state -> linear(1) head, joblib-picklable via __getstate__/__setstate__ routing through state_dict (not raw nn.Module pickling) so a version-drifted torch can still warn rather than silently misload, the same discipline MODEL-FLOW-007-T11's framework_versions field exists to make visible. build_model's lstm/gru branch now constructs it instead of raising. main() gained an is_sequence branch at every step from label-mask through predictions.parquet — windowing, split, fit/predict, holdout scoring (windowed too, not left silently skipped), and a windowed split_spec (method='chronological_windowed') — while the existing 10-algorithm flat path is BYTE-FOR-BYTE unchanged beneath the else (confirmed by the regression run below, not just by inspection). assert_no_nan_features added: a window's inclusion is gated on its TARGET row's label, never its non-target rows' quality, so a NaN feature on an in-window (non-target) row would otherwise train silently to NaN loss — the exact 'looks like success' class this trainer's other guards exist to catch. Dockerfile gained COPY sequence_model.py (missing on the first build attempt — caught before any container ran, via source review) and TMPDIR=/scratch.

THREE real defects found and fixed by this pass's own live verification steps, not by inspection — recorded because each is a genuine trap a future pass touching this image could refall into: (1) torch's default intra-op thread pool sizes off every LOGICAL core the KERNEL reports, which `docker run --cpus=2` does not change (cgroups throttle CPU TIME, not what os.cpu_count() answers) — the FIRST resource-benchmark attempt measured 500 windows x 3 epochs taking OVER 10 MINUTES pegged at ~196% CPU before this was caught and fixed (sequence_model.py: torch.set_num_threads/set_num_interop_threads, capped to the same 2 NanoCpus is set to) — POST-fix, the identical benchmark took 0.39s. (2) RunCompleteSchema.splitSpec was `.strict()` with `method: z.literal('chronological')` only — a windowed run's real /complete call would have 400'd AFTER a successful fit, discovered by inspection during this pass's own investigation (not live) and fixed via SplitSpecSchema, a z.discriminatedUnion('method', [chronological, chronological_windowed]) — chronological_windowed's variant adds sequence_length and documents that its train_rows/test_rows/labelled_rows are WINDOW counts, not row counts (also true of the identically-named metrics.train_rows/test_rows and predictions row_count for this algorithm — stated explicitly wherever those numbers surface, not left to look uniform across all 11 algorithms). apps/client/services/model-draft.ts's ModelRunSplitSpec widened to match (additive, loose-interface style matching this file's own convention). (3) The production container runs ReadonlyRootfs=true with ONLY /scratch writable — /tmp sits on the read-only rootfs. sklearn/lightgbm/xgboost never needed a system temp dir, so this was invisible until the FIRST live end-to-end run through the REAL API-orchestrated container hit `[Errno 2] No usable temporary directory found in ['/tmp', '/var/tmp', '/usr/tmp', '/app']` (torch/joblib's own tempfile use) — NOT caught by this pass's own earlier ad-hoc `docker run` smoke tests, which lacked --read-only and so had a writable /tmp by accident. Fixed via `TMPDIR=/scratch` (pointed at /scratch itself, not a baked-in subdirectory — /scratch is a tmpfs MOUNTED AT CONTAINER RUNTIME that shadows anything baked into the image at that path, so a build-time `mkdir /scratch/tmp` would have been invisible the moment the real tmpfs mounted over it; train.py's own SCRATCH.mkdir(), main()'s first line of work, is what actually guarantees the directory exists before fit() is ever reached). Re-verified clean under FULL production fidelity (--read-only --tmpfs /scratch:...:mode=1777 --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges) before the next live API run was attempted again.

Also caught mid-pass, an operational trap unrelated to the trainer image: `pkill -f "nest start --watch"` does not reliably kill the actual HTTP-listening child process nest's watch mode spawns — a stale backend from an EARLIER restart this session kept answering on :4000 with a stale pinned image digest, causing the first live-run attempt to fail against an image that no longer matched what had just been rebuilt. Fixed by killing via `lsof -ti :4000 | xargs kill -9` instead of a process-name pattern, and by re-confirming `docker inspect <image> --format '{{.Id}}'` matches the backend's own logged 'Training image pinned to...' line before trusting a live run against it — worth keeping as a check for any future pass rebuilding this image mid-session.

Resource benchmark (LSTM_MAX_TRAIN_WINDOWS, full measured comment block now in train.py): measured POST-thread-fix against the real built image via a source-mounted container under production-matching --memory=8g --memory-swap=8g --cpus=2. Unlike GPR's O(n^2) kernel-matrix profile, both wall time AND peak RSS scale roughly LINEARLY with window count — no natural OOM-risk inflection was found anywhere in the tested range (500 to 75,000 windows, hidden_size=64, sequence_length=24, 3 benchmark epochs). 50,000 windows (14.84s, 0.570 GiB peak RSS) was chosen as the ceiling the same way GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS was: the largest value ACTUALLY MEASURED with one further point (75,000: 22.33s, 0.598 GiB) shown safely beyond it, not an extrapolation into unmeasured territory. Extrapolated (linearly, epochs scale linearly) to the wizard's own epochs default of 50: ~247s (~4.1 min) at the ceiling — comfortably inside a background job's patience. Enforced, not just documented: build_model's lstm/gru branch now raises by name if n_train_rows (a WINDOW count for this algorithm) exceeds it, the same enforcement discipline the grp branch already applies to GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS.

LIVE END-TO-END RUN (scripts/verify/model-flow-009-t04-lstm.py, new — same auth/psql/Api helper pattern as model-flow-008-lifecycle.py, reused deliberately rather than reinvented): a real ModelDraft against the 15,441-row S204FBP.lab dataset (dense target — every row Good, unlike the sparse-target unit-test fixture, so this run exercises the SYSTEM end to end while the sparse-spacing correctness claim stays covered by T01's own regression test), PATCHed to algorithm=lstm with sequence_length=24/hidden_size=64/epochs=15/batch_size=64, POSTed as a real run, and polled through a REAL Docker container. ALL 6 STAGES PASSED in 44.7s total (41.1s fit): run f4bdc22c-... SUCCEEDED with a real modelKey; splitSpec.method='chronological_windowed' with sequence_length=24, 12,334 train / 3,084 test windows, accepted by the new discriminated-union schema and correctly persisted; 3,084 real prediction points with row_count matching test_rows exactly; loss_history.json (read directly via ObjectStore, since NO GET .../loss-history route exists for a plain single run — see the real finding immediately below) recorded 15 real per-epoch losses, DECREASING (0.0429 -> 0.0079), proving a genuine fit rather than a no-op. r2=-11.6153 on this real, untuned, unfamiliar dataset — an honest, unfavourable number left unmassaged: 15 epochs with no hyperparameter search is not expected to beat a dataset's own peculiarities, and the pipeline's job (proven by the loss curve) is that training genuinely happened, not that this particular fit is good.

A real, pre-existing scope gap surfaced by writing the live-run script, NOT introduced by this task and NOT fixed here (out of scope — it affects every algorithm with a loss curve equally, not lstm/gru specifically): getRunLossHistory (python-preprocess-client.ts) is only ever called from model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts, embedding a candidate's lossHistory into ITS OWN response — there is no GET route exposing a PLAIN single run's loss_history.json to a caller at all. mlp/hgb/lightgbm/xgboost have had this exact gap since MODEL-FLOW-013-T05; lstm/gru simply inherit it. Left for whoever picks up that gap next, named explicitly rather than silently worked around.

tasks.title: Design the windowing step (2D -> 3D) and where it runs in the pipeline
tasks.detail: Sequence models need (samples, timesteps, features); train.py currently builds a flat (samples, features) frame and hands feature_cols straight to fit(). Windowing must happen BEFORE chronological_split (train.py:143-164) — windowing after the split lets a window's timesteps span the train/test boundary, which is exactly the ordering bug the module docstring already warns about for the non-Good-target drop (train.py:8-12), just one step later in the pipeline.
tasks.notes: build_windows added (train.py, directly after chronological_split) — pure pandas/numpy, 5 unit tests (test_train.py), including a regression test proving it windows the FULL frame's true spacing rather than the labelled-only frame the original task framing implied. NOT wired into main()'s live call order this pass — see feature-level implementation note. AC 1's 'runs strictly before chronological_split' is met as file/design order and as the function's own documented precondition, not yet as a live main() execution order, which is T04's job. UPDATE 2026-08-31 (T04): wired into main()'s live is_sequence branch and exercised by a real end-to-end run — AC 1 is now fully MET, not merely file-order MET.

tasks.title: Extend the leakage guard to cover window-straddling, not just row-wise lags
tasks.detail: assert_no_target_leakage (train.py:101-140) reasons about row-wise lag features via the target's labelled-vs-row median sampling gap — it says nothing about a WINDOW that starts before the cut and ends after it. A window straddling chronological_split's boundary is a leakage path today's guard cannot see, because it was written for a different failure shape (a lag column repeating the current target value, not a window spanning two sides of a split). This needs its own check, not a parameter on the existing one.
tasks.notes: assert_no_window_leakage added as its own function (not a parameter on assert_no_target_leakage, per this task's own instruction) alongside chronological_split_windows. Turned out to be ONE assertion, not new analysis, once windows are correctly target-keyed (build_windows guarantees this) — a train window's target timestamp is provably always pre-cut by construction, so the guard's real job is catching an implementation mistake (start-index vs target-index assignment), which its own test deliberately simulates and confirms is caught.

tasks.title: Add sequence_length (and validate epochs/batch_size/hidden_size against it) to the hyperparameter contract
tasks.detail: Correction to an earlier framing of this gap: HYPERPARAMS.lstm / HYPERPARAMS.gru (apps/client/lib/training-config.ts:212-264) already collect epochs, batch_size, and hidden_size — those are NOT missing. The one genuinely missing field is sequence_length, the value that actually defines the window this feature needs. Both the DTO's HyperparametersSchema and the client catalogue need it added, and epochs/batch_size need a documented default now that they will actually be consumed by a real fit loop instead of sitting unused.
tasks.notes: sequence_length added to HYPERPARAMS.lstm/.gru (default 24, min 1) with the pinned-key-set test updated. DTO needed no edit — HyperparametersSchema is already a generic scalar record and accepts it as-is (confirmed by reading the current file, not assumed from the task's own framing). epochs/batch_size/hidden_size already had defaults from the earlier tabular-algorithm pass; no new validation added against sequence_length specifically since no fit loop exists yet to validate against (T04). UPDATE 2026-08-31 (T04): the fit loop now exists (SequenceRegressor) and a real end-to-end run confirmed sequence_length/hidden_size/epochs/batch_size all round-trip from the client catalogue's defaults through to the persisted splitSpec/manifest correctly — no additional cross-field validation was found necessary beyond what already existed.

That audit's 'not a defect to fix' conclusion was reached against the current sklearn-only image; it does not automatically extend to an image carrying a full DL framework and this needs its own pass, not an inherited one.
tasks.note: Built and LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-31 (same session, second pass) — full account in the feature-level implementation note's '=== T04 ===' section. torch 2.5.1 CPU-only added; sequence_model.py (SequenceRegressor) built; build_windows/chronological_split_windows/assert_no_window_leakage wired into main()'s live is_sequence branch (windowing, split, fit/predict, WINDOWED holdout scoring, windowed split_spec) while the flat 10-algorithm path stays byte-for-byte unchanged (regression-proven, not just inspected); assert_no_nan_features added, closing the NaN-in-window gap this task's own note flagged; RunCompleteSchema.splitSpec's strictness gap (also flagged here) fixed via a discriminated union; resource sizing re-audited and LIVE-MEASURED (not assumed) — linear, not quadratic, scaling, 50,000-window ceiling enforced by name; TrainingAlgorithmEnum + algorithm-selector.tsx unblocked; one real end-to-end lstm run SUCCEEDED through the real API/container. The RunManifestSchema concern this note raised was checked and found moot: framework_versions is the only field that schema reads, unaffected by split_spec's shape. The chronological_split_windows-cuts-on-window-count-vs-chronological_split-cuts-on-row-count gap this note also raised is REAL and UNRESOLVED — recorded here for whoever next puts an lstm/gru candidate beside a tabular one in a MODEL-FLOW-013 candidate set, since that is the first place differently-timed test-set RMSEs would actually need reconciling; out of this task's own scope (a single-algorithm live run) to design.
