features.title: New Step 2 — Dataset Review before Training Configuration
features.description: A review step between Model Setup and Training Configuration. Shows which data source the selected dataset came from, its per-tag statistics, the same DataAnalysisCard the dataset wizard's Step 3.1 uses, and the held-out validation window — so an engineer sees WHAT they are about to train on before configuring HOW. Includes a route back into the dataset wizard for a dataset that needs changing.
userDecisions: STEP COUNT (resolved): five steps. The flow becomes Setup -> Dataset Review -> Training Configuration -> Evaluation -> Save Model. This file's global_definition_of_done currently asserts four steps in four separate lines and MODEL-FLOW-008 verifies by step number; all of them are rewritten as part of T01 rather than left to contradict the feature that renumbered them.

EDIT DATASET RE-ENTRY (resolved): warn-and-navigate, NOT an overlay and NOT a full URL-addressable resume. An overlay would keep the model wizard mounted and make Back a close rather than a rehydration — genuinely smaller than a resume mechanism — but it rests on three unverified assumptions about the dataset wizard (mountable outside its route, no atom collision, no reset-on-mount). Three unknowns for one button is a poor trade against an honest dialog. The draft is PATCHed current before navigating and is resumable from the models list (T08).
findings: RESTORED 2026-08-25. This array was found holding six MODEL-SERVE findings (run_manifest.json / serving bundle / artifact pinning / one bucket / MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 / checksum sidecar) — verbatim duplicates of MODEL-SERVE.findings, and this feature's own five findings were gone. Six pointers in this same feature (T05, T07's detail AND its note, V02, and acceptance criteria 3 and 5) resolve to them, so every one of those was reading a finding about serving. The serving findings live in MODEL-SERVE and are removed here. The originals are restored below from what those six pointers assert about them; wording is reconstructed, the claims are not.

DATAANALYSISCARD WAS DRAFT-SCOPED, THEN MADE STORE-AGNOSTIC (two reversals, both kept visible). Originally judged 'reusable but type-gated' — wrong on three counts: it read dwDraftIdAtom/dwDraftArtifactIdAtom/dwDraftGoldArtifactIdAtom directly; its histogram/boxplot/scatter tabs hit DRAFT-scoped routes with no datasetId-scoped twin (only correlation had one); and it rendered FeatureTransformDialog, a write to dwScalerConfigsAtom, inside a step that configures nothing. RESOLVED 2026-08-20: compose instead of reuse. REVERSED 2026-08-21 on explicit user request: the card is mounted after all, but only after all three defects were fixed at source — optional datasetId/artifactId props short-circuit the dw* routing, showTransforms={false} suppresses the dialog and stops it inheriting dwScalerConfigsAtom. What remains shared is dwHiddenTagsAtom/dwFocusedTagAtom via useDatasetTagSelection — view state, accepted knowingly. Dropped in unmodified, four of six tabs would have shown 'pending' forever.

THE STEP HOLDS NO SERVER STATE OF ITS OWN. It reads the dataset's committed artifact and configures nothing. ModelDraft needs no new column and receives no PATCH from this step — stated up front so it is not given one by reflex. (T07 later carved out ONE exception, the user-confirmed Edit Dataset flush; see acceptance criterion 3.)

EDITING A DATASET DOES NOT REMOVE IT. The Dataset row keeps its id; what changes is currentArtifactId, and possibly the tag list. So datasetId on the ModelDraft stays valid across an edit and must NOT be cleared. What genuinely goes stale is the selected TARGET, if the edit dropped that tag — a different field with a different consequence.

RESUME IS THE ONLY RETURN PATH THAT PRESERVES ANYTHING (T07/T08). Browser Back re-mounts the wizard with no ?draftId=, and useModelWizardMode's create branch calls reset() unconditionally — so Back wipes the jotai atoms even though the server row survives. That is why the hand-off dialog says so outright, and why reconciliation lives in the resume branch rather than a general on-return hook: there is no other return.

tasks.title: Validation-holdout panel
tasks.detail:
CORRECTED SCOPE 2026-08-20: checked against the code and the holdout's missing/Bad rate exists NOWHERE — not on DatasetArtifact, not in ArtifactStatsSchema/ArtifactStats, not computed anywhere in artifact_service.py. The holdout window itself also has no client-facing read path: it lives on the BRONZE sibling of the run's GOLD/FINAL artifact, resolved by runId — the same lookup tryReplayHoldout (model-run.authorized.service.ts) already does server-side, never exposed to a browser. This is a real build, not a composition of existing reads:

1. Python — artifact_service.py's materialize() holdout branch and resplit_holdout() both already hold validate_frame in memory; pass missing_pct(validate_frame) (object_store.py) into _stats_payload as a new validation_missing_pct field. ArtifactStatsResponse (schemas/preprocess.py) gains the field, nullable/optional like validation_row_count beside it.
2. Prisma — DatasetArtifact.validationMissingPct Float?, migrated.
3. Backend — ArtifactStatsSchema (dataset-version.authorized.dto.ts) gains validation_missing_pct; persisted in both places that already set validationRowCount (dataset-version.authorized.service.ts and dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts).
4. New read endpoint GET /datasets/:id/artifacts/:artifactId/holdout: resolve the artifact's runId, find its BRONZE sibling, and if validationRowCount is set return {holdoutFrom, holdoutTo, rowCount, missingPct} — window bounds from Python /metadata against validateDataKey (footer-only, bounded), missingPct from the new column.

THE MISSING RATE IS NOT OPTIONAL for any holdout captured going forward. A holdout written before this change returns missingPct: null, and the panel says so plainly ('missing rate not recorded for this holdout') rather than omitting the field silently or inventing a compute-on-read scan (which would defeat the bounded-read discipline V03 checks). DS-LAKE-018's resolved no-imputation decision means the holdout stays raw, so a MISSING_VALUE hole reaches predict() and depresses the score with no trace of why; its own T05 already requires the rate be published beside every metric for that reason.
tasks.note: Completed 2026-08-20, all 4 layers plus the new read endpoint. Python: artifact_service.py's _stats_payload/_commit/materialize/resplit_holdout all gained validation_missing_pct, computed via missing_pct(validate_frame) while the frame is already in memory; ArtifactStatsResponse (schemas/preprocess.py) gained the matching nullable field. Prisma: DatasetArtifact.validationMissingPct Float?, migrated via `pnpm db:migrate:dev` (migration model_flow_010_t06_validation_missing_pct) then `pnpm --filter=@softsensor/prisma build` to regenerate the dist Client the backend actually imports (the raw `prisma generate` alone left the backend's compiled @softsensor/prisma types stale — 5 TS2353/TS2339 errors until the package build ran). Backend: ArtifactStatsSchema gained validation_missing_pct; persisted at all THREE call sites that set validationRowCount (dataset-version.authorized.service.ts:497, dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts:320 and :502 — one more site than the task's original 2-site plan). New GET /datasets/:id/artifacts/:artifactId/holdout (getArtifactHoldoutService/-Controller): resolves the BRONZE sibling by runId, returns {holdout: null} with HTTP 200 (not 404 — 'no holdout' is the common case here, not exceptional) when validationRowCount/validationHoldoutFrom are unset, else {holdoutFrom, holdoutTo, rowCount, missingPct} with holdoutTo derived from a Python /metadata footer-only call against validateDataKey (holdout_to itself is never persisted). Client: datasetArtifactService.holdout() + useArtifactHoldout hook (hooks/dataset/artifact/ — the subdirectory concurrent DS-LAKE holdout work had already moved the sibling hooks into) + HoldoutPanel showing the window/rows/missing-rate trio, with 'missing rate not recorded for this holdout' for a legacy null. Tests added beyond the original plan: a Python pytest (test_artifact_service_resplit_holdout.py) asserting validation_missing_pct == missing_pct(validate_frame) for a frame with known Bad cells (2/10 -> 20%); a Nest spec (dataset-version.authorized.service.spec.ts) covering BRONZE-found, no-holdout, legacy-null-missingPct and not-found — all passing.

DEFERRED 2026-08-20: out of scope for the T01-T06 pass (composition of the review step itself). Explicitly NOT started because its own dialog-copy rule below is coupled to T08 shipping, and T08 has not. When picked up: PATCH the draft to current BEFORE navigating. useModelDraftSync's PATCH is 600ms-debounced, so a click landing inside that window leaves the server row stale; ensureDraftId already exists for this class of 'the server must know before we do something irreversible' problem.

DO NOT clear datasetId — see findings. Clearing it would discard a reference that stayed valid and force the user to re-pick something that never changed.

RECONCILE ON RETURN, by whatever path: re-fetch the dataset, invalidate every artifact-keyed hook, and CHECK THE TARGET STILL EXISTS in the new artifact's tag list. A dropped target surviving in mpTargetVariableAtom fails at run creation with a pyarrow 'No match for FieldRef.Name' error that names a column and explains nothing — the same class of failure the Step 3.1 correlation tab already hit once.

DIALOG COPY MUST MATCH WHAT SHIPS: it may claim the draft is saved and resumable only if T08 ships. If T08 is cut, the copy says the configuration is discarded. A dialog promising a resume nothing can honour is worse than one admitting the loss.
tasks.note:
Completed 2026-08-21. The Edit Dataset button + AlertDialog live in phase-2-dataset-review.tsx, but the flush-then-navigate ORDER — the only part that can be got wrong invisibly — lives in hooks/model/use-dataset-edit-handoff.ts, so it is testable and the step stays a composition shell.

useModelDraftSync gained `{ autoSync }` (default true, so phase-2-training-config is untouched) and `flush()`. One shared `syncNow` writer now backs both the debounced effect and the explicit flush; flush cancels the armed 600ms debounce first (leaving it armed would re-send the same body after the user has already navigated) and, unlike the effect, it THROWS — so a failed PATCH aborts the navigation, keeps the user on the step and surfaces a toast. The review step passes autoSync:false, so finding #3 still holds exactly as written for mount and for every control in the step; acceptance criterion 3 was REWORDED to carve out the user-confirmed hand-off rather than left asserting something the code no longer does.

datasetId is NOT cleared, per the findings. The seed-and-navigate itself was extracted out of useDataStudio.handleDatasetEdit into hooks/dataset/use-dataset-edit-navigation.ts and both callers now share one implementation — that indirection is also what keeps V02's store/dataset-studio ban intact, since the hand-off needs initDatasetWizardForEditAtom and the step itself still imports no dw* atom.

RECONCILE-ON-RETURN landed in the resume path (T08), which is the only return path that preserves anything: browser Back re-mounts useModelWizardMode with no draftId and hits its reset(). Resume re-fetches the dataset, and that re-fetch IS the artifact-hook invalidation — useArtifactMetadata / useArtifactColumnStats / useArtifactRows / useArtifactHoldout are each keyed on (datasetId, artifactId), and the metadata module cache keys `${ownerId}:${artifactId}`, so a currentArtifactId moved by the edit is a new key in all four (checked in each file, not assumed). reconcileTarget then clears a target the edit dropped and the toast NAMES it.

DIALOG COPY MATCHES WHAT SHIPS: it claims the draft is saved and resumable, and says plainly that the browser Back button will not restore it. UPDATED 2026-08-21 with T08's relocation — it now names New Model -> Step 1 -> Drafts in progress rather than Models -> Drafts in progress, because that is where the panel actually is. A dialog pointing at a screen that no longer holds the thing it promises is the same defect as promising a resume nothing can honour.

tasks.title: Resume an ACTIVE ModelDraft from the models list
tasks.detail: DEFERRED 2026-08-20, out of scope for the T01-T06 pass. CORRECTED CLAIM: the prior detail here said 'the draft row already holds every field the wizard would restore' — checked against packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma's ModelDraft model and that is false. It has name/workspaceId/plantId/nodeId/datasetId/targetY/algorithm/hyperparameters/splitRatio/status/currentRunId — no description, no algorithms[] (multi-algorithm selection), no lossFunction, no selectedMetrics, no deploy config (autoRetrain/warnSd/criticalSd/driftMonitor/driftThresholdPct). Restore from this row is PARTIAL. The controller (model-draft.authorized.controller.ts) also has no list route yet — only POST, GET /:id, PATCH /:id, POST /:id/abandon; a GET /model-drafts?workspaceId=&status=ACTIVE is needed first. The step-position part of this task is still fine as originally scoped (derivable from status + currentRunId, no schema change) — only the 'every field' claim was wrong. When picked up, the resume dialog/toast must say what actually restores, not imply full parity.
tasks.note:
Completed 2026-08-21. Backend: GET /authorized/model-drafts, declared BEFORE @Get('/:id') because Nest matches in declaration order and a bare GET would otherwise never be reached; ListModelDraftQueryDto {workspaceId?, status?}. The owner-or-member workspace clause was extracted into a private workspaceScope(user) now shared by assertWorkspaceAccess, assertDraftAccess and the list — a second hand-written copy is how a list ends up broader than the GET it links to. An inaccessible workspaceId 404s rather than returning [] ('not yours' is a different fact from 'none here'). `status` accepts the full enum deliberately and the UI asks for ACTIVE. New spec model-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts (the module had none), 7/7 passing: scope-applied-with-no-filters, both filters, the 404, the ADMIN bypass keeping deletedAt, ISO dates + splitRatio still a FRACTION, and — because workspaceScope now backs the other three routes too — a direct comparison proving the list's WHERE.workspace is the SAME object shape assertDraftAccess builds, plus a 404 for a draft that clause filters out. Two clauses that merely agree today would pass a per-method test and diverge later.

Client: modelDraftService.list; useModelDrafts (plain local state, not useAllModels' shared-atom + module-dedup shape — one consumer, one request; a failed load hides the panel instead of erroring the page); DraftResumePanel, which renders NOTHING when there are no drafts. REVISED 2026-08-21 ON USER REQUEST: it now carries THREE ways to clear drafts as well as Resume — a per-row X, Remove selected (a checkbox per row, shown only once something is ticked), and Remove all. The remove had been withheld as MODEL-FLOW-011's, which was the wrong call for this surface — a list that only ever grows is a list people stop reading, and it sits in the wizard now, not on an admin page. It ABANDONS (POST /:id/abandon, already built): status ACTIVE -> ABANDONED, training runs untouched, so the copy says 'removed from this list', never 'deleted'. All three share ONE confirm, differing only in which drafts they hand it — three dialogs would be three copies of the same wording to keep in step — and it is confirmed rather than immediate, matching how ModelTable guards its own row-level destructive action: the X sits one mis-click from Resume, Remove all is one click from everything, and there is no undo anywhere in the UI. The dialog is held open until the server confirms, so a failed remove cannot close over rows that stayed.

No bulk endpoint was invented for this: the confirm fans out one abandon per draft and settles them all, because a bulk route that abandons some rows and fails on others has the SAME partial outcome to report — it would just hide it behind one status code. Partial failure is therefore a real state and is handled as one: all-failed keeps the dialog open and says so, some-failed closes, refetches and names the count that did not go. Selection is held by id and resolved against the current list each render, so an id whose draft has since left the list (resumed, or removed in another tab) cannot produce a 'Remove selected (1)' that removes nothing. Reclaiming the ABANDONED rows themselves is still MODEL-FLOW-011.

The list caps at 5 rows and scrolls past that (ScrollArea, fixed height): unbounded, it would push the preset picker and the dataset grid off a laptop screen, which is the opposite of what a 'pick up where you left off' affordance should do. Nothing is truncated — every draft stays reachable. The icon-only X takes an aria-label naming its draft, or a screen reader hears five identical 'remove' buttons.

RELOCATED 2026-08-21 ON USER REQUEST: the panel now sits at the TOP OF STEP 1, directly above the preset picker, not on /models/views — picking up unfinished work is a different intent from starting new, and it belongs before the choices that assume you are starting new. That move broke the mechanism, not just the placement: Resume used to push /models/create?draftId=..., which is INERT from inside the wizard (already mounted on that route, so useModelWizardMode's run-once effect never sees the changed query) — a dead button that typechecks. So the restore logic was extracted out of that effect into hooks/model/use-model-draft-resume.ts, which both entries now share: the URL keeps working on a cold mount, and Step 1 hydrates IN PLACE. Failure no longer navigates from inside the hook — the URL caller sends the user back to /models/views, the in-wizard caller leaves them where they are, because nothing was lost. Either way it is a CREATE-mode continuation, not a mode of its own, since no Model row exists yet.

Two consequences of living inside the wizard, both handled: resuming now REPLACES work the user may already have typed (impossible on the models list), so DraftResumeSection confirms first when the wizard is dirty — a name typed or a dataset chosen — and the draft already open is filtered out of its own list. New test pipeline/__tests__/draft-resume-section.test.tsx, 16/16: in-place hydrate on a clean wizard, the confirm on a dirty one, dismissal leaving it alone, the current draft not offered, nothing rendered when there are no drafts, remove confirming-then-abandoning and refetching, cancel and failure leaving the draft in place, the per-draft aria-label, the 5-row cap (no scroll container at 5, one at 6, with all 6 still reachable), Remove all abandoning every listed draft, Remove selected abandoning ONLY the ticked ones (the unticked row must survive), unticking shrinking the count, a partial failure reported rather than passed off as success, and an all-failed batch keeping the dialog open without refetching.

RESTORE IS PARTIAL AND SAYS SO, per this task's own corrected claim: the row has no description, algorithms[], lossFunction, selectedMetrics or deploy config, so the toast states exactly what came back rather than implying parity. Hydration uses RAW atom setters, never useModelPipelineNav's — every one of those calls resetTraining() and relocks highestUnlocked, and setAlgorithm additionally overwrites hyperparameters with that algorithm's defaults, which would have discarded the draft's stored set moments after restoring it. Step position: land on Step 1 so the restored choices are confirmed, unlock to 2 once the dataset resolves and NO FURTHER, because no training result is restored and an empty Evaluation step would be a lie. splitRatio fraction -> percent, and algorithm/hyperparameters are narrowed by type guard in lib/model-draft-hydration.ts rather than cast.

THREE GAPS, STATED NOT HIDDEN. (1) A TRAINED draft is reachable through the API but is not offered in the panel, because its run result is not rebuilt on resume. (2) Leaving via browser Back and starting over can leave an extra ACTIVE draft behind; reclaiming those is MODEL-FLOW-011, not this task. (3) resumeDraft does not check status: a hand-edited ?draftId= or a panel rendered before another tab saved that draft can resume a SAVED row, whose every later PATCH 409s into the debounced sync's silent catch — so the user would configure against a row that refuses updates. Narrow (the panel refetches on mount and nothing in the UI abandons a draft) and it is lifecycle territory, so it is recorded here for MODEL-FLOW-011 rather than guarded now.

acceptance_criteria: The wizard has five steps, and this file's own definition of done says five rather than still claiming four.
No existing step's behaviour changes — only its number.

The review step reads the dataset's committed artifact and configures nothing; ModelDraft gains no column, and nothing in the step PATCHes it — not on mount, not from any control. REVISED 2026-08-21 (T07): the single exception is the Edit Dataset hand-off, which flushes the draft ONCE, after the user confirms the dialog, because criterion 8 requires the draft be persisted before leaving. That is the user walking out of the step, not the step configuring anything — enforced by passing autoSync:false to useModelDraftSync, so the debounced writer never runs here at all.
Per-tag statistics are served from the sidecar without opening data.parquet.

The review step's preview comes from a bounded server page (useArtifactRows: 200 rows x 50 tags); the step reads no dw* atom and mounts no dataset-wizard mutation UI. REVISED AGAIN 2026-08-21 (user request): the step now DOES mount DataAnalysisCard, but only after that component was made store-agnostic — it is passed an explicit datasetId/artifactId so every server-backed tab routes through the dataset-scoped artifact routes with no dw* atom deciding anything, and showTransforms={false} keeps FeatureTransformDialog (a WRITE to dwScalerConfigsAtom) out of a step that configures nothing. The 'no mutation UI' half of this criterion is therefore intact; only the 'compose instead of reuse' means of achieving it changed.
A dataset with no committed artifact shows one honest empty state, not four independent ones.
The holdout panel publishes the holdout's missing/Bad rate beside every figure it shows.
Leaving to edit a dataset persists the draft first, and the dialog states exactly what survives.
Returning after an edit re-reads the dataset and clears a target the edit removed, saying so.
An ACTIVE ModelDraft is reachable from the models list.

features.title: ModelDraft Lifecycle Reclaim
features.description: DS-LAKE-014 gave DatasetDraft a sweeper and closed the never-abandoned-ACTIVE hole for datasets. ModelDraft is a separate table with no equivalent, so the identical leak exists here: a user who closes the tab leaves an ACTIVE ModelDraft forever, because nothing calls /abandon on their behalf.
findings: DELIBERATELY NOT A TASK INSIDE MODEL-FLOW-002. That feature is completed at 100% with nine live-verified tasks; reopening it to add reclaim work would make its own completion claim false and mix verified history with unstarted work. The concerns are also independent — 002 gives the container a row to read, this decides when an unused row is released, and neither constrains the other. The DS-LAKE side already answered this question the same way: the DatasetDraft entity is DS-LAKE-005 and its sweeper is DS-LAKE-014, nine features apart.

THE STORAGE COST IS SMALLER THAN THE DATASET CASE BUT NOT ZERO. A ModelDraft owns no artifact of its own, so an abandoned one leaks a Postgres row rather than object bytes. Its ModelTrainingRuns DO write under drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/ (MODEL-FLOW-003-T08), and nothing reclaims those today — so the leak is real, just concentrated in the runs rather than the draft.

MODEL-FLOW-010-T07 MAKES THIS MORE FREQUENT, NOT MERELY MORE VISIBLE. Leaving the wizard to edit a dataset becomes a normal, encouraged action there; every user who does not come back leaves an ACTIVE draft behind. The leak predates that feature but its rate does not.

MODEL-FLOW-013 MULTIPLIES THIS FEATURE'S LEAK RATE, IT DOES NOT CREATE IT (2026-08-28). A candidate job (algorithm sweep or hyperparameter search) with N candidates now writes N run prefixes under drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/ where the flow previously wrote one per draft. This feature's own T02 finding (the reclaim unit is the RUN, not the draft) already anticipated the multi-run case and needs no change for it — what changes is that N-runs-per-draft becomes the COMMON case (any 'Find Best Model' sweep) rather than an observed accident. T05's own instruction (never reclaim a prefix an adopted run points at) also already covers a candidate job's bestRunId/selectedRunId correctly, since those are just ModelTrainingRun ids like any other.

MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-31, BEFORE ANY CODE: TRAINED drafts hold 11.0 of 11.3 MB of all draft-run bytes in MinIO; ACTIVE held 0.3 MB, ABANDONED 0. T01's own rule — TRAINED is never eligible on either window — is correct (Save Model consumes it) but means this feature reclaims almost none of the actually-leaking bytes. Recorded, not fixed here: a TRAINED-draft retention class belongs to MODEL-SERVE-007 ('Retention Classes in Object Storage'), per user decision this session.

drafts/ IS A SHARED ROOT FOR TWO UNRELATED ENTITIES, CONFIRMED LIVE. 14 model-draft prefixes and 6 dataset-draft prefixes coexist under drafts/ in the one `datasets` bucket, discriminated only by the third path segment (runs/ vs artifacts/). is_draft_run_key (MODEL-FLOW-000-T09) is filename-terminated only and cannot validate a directory prefix — T02 added is_draft_run_prefix specifically so this sweep's delete_prefix calls are structurally unable to reach a DatasetDraft's artifacts/ objects, never a bare drafts/{id}/.

9 RUN PREFIXES IN MinIO HAD NO ModelTrainingRun ROW AT ALL, measured live before this pass (under ACTIVE drafts 24d6c4a2 and d8909c20). A row-driven per-run delete (T02's literal wording) could never reach these — they were bytes whose row was already gone by some earlier, unrelated path. T02 was built as a subtree delete whenever no run on a draft is adopted, which catches this case for free; both drafts' run objects were confirmed live-deleted in this pass (12 and 16 objects respectively).

T05'S GUARD IS CURRENTLY UNSATISFIABLE BY DATA — RECORDED, NOT A DEFECT. Zero ModelTrainingRun rows have modelId set anywhere in the dataset (confirmed live via a full-table check); Save Model's adopt-by-pointer write is MODEL-FLOW-007-T10, unbuilt. The per-run filter (never name a run whose modelId is set) is implemented and unit-tested — including a live Python MinIO test that writes two run prefixes and proves the untouched sibling stays readable after its neighbour is reclaimed — but has no real adopted row to prove itself against yet. This must ship BEFORE -007, not after, or -007's very first adoption is unguarded for one release.

THE OPEN-TAB HAZARD (found during design, fixed in this pass, not in the original 5 tasks). patchDraftService 409'd only on SAVED; assertDraftWritableStatus (Start Training) already refused ABANDONED. A draft the sweep abandoned while a wizard tab sat open kept accepting the debounced PATCH into useModelDraftSync's silent catch — the user would only learn at Start Training, the one irreversible step. Fixed: patchDraftService now 409s on ABANDONED too, so the very next edit surfaces it.

T04 COVERS RUNNING, NOT QUEUED. A run that never reaches spawn() (e.g. the backend dies between the DB write and the Docker call) stays QUEUED forever with no containerId to check against — outside this task's literal wording ('for each RUNNING run'). Not fixed here; recorded as a gap for whoever next touches run-launch reliability.

PRE-EXISTING, UNRELATED DB-MIGRATION DRIFT WAS HIT AND RESOLVED DURING THIS PASS. Two migrations already on disk (20260827120000_model_flow_013_candidate_job, 20260828140000_model_flow_013_t11_sweep_then_tune) had been applied to the dev DB via `prisma db execute` rather than `prisma migrate dev` — both migration files say so themselves, citing a DatasetArtifact.droppedBadRows drift with no migration file, present before this feature started. `prisma migrate dev` refused to run at all until both were marked applied via `prisma migrate resolve --applied` (bookkeeping only, no SQL, confirmed via `prisma migrate diff` showing only this feature's own ALTER TABLE afterward). T01's own migration (20260831180000) was then applied the same way DS-LAKE-013 already documents as this project's own established path around that pre-existing drift.

tasks.title: Tiered ACTIVE-draft eligibility for ModelDraft
tasks.detail: Mirror DS-LAKE-014's tiers rather than inventing a second policy: a draft owning ZERO runs releases on a short window (nothing was computed, nothing is expensive to lose); a draft owning runs releases on a long idle window (a real fit cost minutes of container time). Measure from updatedAt, the same convention DS-LAKE-014's branches use and the same one DS-LAKE-009B-T08 already had to fix once by moving OFF artifact.createdAt. A TRAINED draft is NOT eligible on either window — it holds a finished result the user may still be reviewing in Step 4, which is exactly the state Save Model consumes.
tasks.note:
Completed 2026-08-31. lib/model-draft-cleanup-eligibility.ts, reportModelDraftEligibility, pure (no Prisma/I-O, `now` a parameter): emptyIdleHours=24 (not DS-LAKE-014's 15 min — an abandoned draft drops off Step 1's resume panel, so the whole grace period matters here, not just byte cost), runsIdleHours=168, plus a THIRD tier T01's text does not name — abandonedRecoveryHours=168 for an already-ABANDONED draft with unreclaimed bytes (covers MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's Remove button, which flips status with no byte cleanup). New ModelDraft.objectsReclaimedAt DateTime? (nullable, mirrors DatasetArtifact.objectReclaimedAt) added via migration 20260831180000_model_flow_011_t01_objects_reclaimed_at.

TWO GUARDS BEYOND T01'S TEXT, BOTH LOAD-BEARING: any run QUEUED/RUNNING, or any ModelCandidateJob QUEUED/RUNNING, skips the draft regardless of age — ModelDraft.updatedAt never moves once a run launches (launchDraftRun writes currentRunId at launch and nothing after), so without this a slow fit inside the window is reclaimable mid-flight. Applied uniformly to ACTIVE and ABANDONED, since abandonDraftService has no guard against abandoning a draft with a live run.

15/15 unit tests (model-draft-cleanup-eligibility.spec.ts), covering every tier and skip reason. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-31 against real Postgres — see V01/V02.

tasks.title: Reclaim the runs' object prefixes, not only the rows
tasks.detail: Abandoning a draft must also release drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/ for each of its runs — otherwise the row disappears and its bytes stay, which is the worse half of the leak and the half nothing currently addresses. is_draft_run_key (MODEL-FLOW-000-T09, MODEL-FLOW-003-T08) is the structural guard that makes a prefix delete safe here; use it rather than a string prefix match.
tasks.note:
Completed 2026-08-31. is_draft_run_key is filename-terminated (4 non-empty segments) and rejects a bare directory prefix by its own empty-trailing-segment rule — reused as-is it would reject every prefix this task needs to delete. New is_draft_run_prefix (object_store.py) is the directory-terminated twin: accepts exactly drafts/{d}/runs/ (2 segments) or drafts/{d}/runs/{r}/ (3), never a bare drafts/{d}/ — the guard that makes this sweep structurally unable to reach a DatasetDraft's artifacts/ objects sharing the same root (see findings). New draft_runs_prefix builder beside draft_run_prefix.

USER DECISION, NOT T02'S LITERAL WORDING: subtree delete (one call, no run_id) when NO run on the draft is adopted — covers the 9 orphan prefixes found live with no ModelTrainingRun row, which a strict per-run delete could never reach. Per-run delete only when some runs ARE adopted (T05). New endpoint POST /v1/preprocess/models/runs/reclaim (DraftRunReclaimRequest{draft_id, run_id?}, validated: bare path segments only, resolved prefix re-checked against is_draft_run_prefix) → reclaim_draft_runs → the existing delete_prefix (unchanged, already idempotent). NestJS has no S3 client (confirmed) — all deletes route through Python, same as the DS-LAKE-014 precedent.

5 Python unit tests (RecordingStore) + 4 live-MinIO tests in test_object_store.py (accept/reject table, non-zero-delete, the T05 sibling-survives proof, subtree-removes-orphan). LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-31 against real MinIO — see V03 (12 and 16 objects actually deleted, confirmed gone via `ls`).

tasks.title: Periodic sweep caller
tasks.detail: setInterval(...).unref() in onModuleInit, matching DS-LAKE-014's chosen mechanism and PreprocessingJobService.scheduleStragglerSweep's existing precedent — not @nestjs/schedule, which would introduce a second scheduling idiom for one interval. Env-configurable with <= 0 disabling it. Errors logged and swallowed: a failed sweep must never crash the app, and anything it would have reclaimed stays eligible for the next tick.
tasks.note:
Completed 2026-08-31. CORRECTED PREMISE, found during design: scheduleStragglerSweep is a one-shot setTimeout with no env config and no query — only its .unref()/swallow-errors idiom is shared; the full onModuleInit+setInterval+onApplicationShutdown+env-disable shape this task specifies is ArtifactCleanupAdminService's alone, copied verbatim. tasks.title: Reconcile orphaned RUNNING runs at boot
tasks.detail: Found during MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's live verification, not in the original scope: run 562ec955 sat at RUNNING with zero log lines after a nest --watch restart killed watch()'s in-memory tracker mid-flight. The container is independent of the Node process, so nothing reconciles a run whose watcher died. That row is now permanently RUNNING — never terminal, so never eligible under any window this feature adds. Reconcile at boot: for each RUNNING run, check whether its container still exists and mark it FAILED with a stated reason if not.
tasks.note:
Completed 2026-08-31. trainning-container.authorized.service.ts's onModuleInit now calls resolveDigest() then the new reconcileOrphanedRuns(). Per RUNNING row: no containerId -> FAILED ('never spawned'); getContainer(id).inspect() throws -> FAILED naming the container id and 'server restarted while this run was in flight'; container still exists -> re-attach void this.watch(runId, container) rather than duplicating its exit-code logic — container.wait() resolves immediately for an already-exited container, so ONE call covers both 'still running' and 'exited while down' through the SAME branch the live watcher uses. Deliberately NOT the blanket updateMany(...) PreprocessingJobService/LoaderJobService use for their own boot sweeps — a training container outlives a nest --watch restart, so a blanket fail would kill runs that were never actually orphaned.

The existing spec was a 20-line CLI stub with no PrismaService and one 'should be defined' assertion — rewritten, 7/7: no-containerId, container-gone, container-still-running-re-attached-not-failed, container-already-exited-reaches-FAILED-through-the-real-watch()-branch (not a mock, proving code reuse), and multi-run independence. Required a fix to a pre-existing gap unrelated to this task's scope: apps/backend/src/types/dockerode.d.ts's hand-rolled Container interface never declared inspect() — added, minimal (Id/State.Running only, the fields this code actually reads).

LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-31 — see V04: run 562ec955, RUNNING since 2026-08-19 with container 1852c38628b8 already confirmed gone from the daemon, reached FAILED with the exact predicted reason on this feature's own real boot, no synthetic setup needed.

tasks.title: Never reclaim a prefix an adopted run points at
tasks.detail:
T01's eligibility tiers exclude a TRAINED draft and say nothing about a SAVED one; T02 deletes drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/ 'for each of its runs'. Read together with MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 — which adopts the winning run BY POINTER and leaves its bytes under the draft prefix forever — those two sentences describe a sweep that can delete the object a saved, possibly deployed, model loads from.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE WEAK ONE. Excluding status=SAVED is necessary and not sufficient: a draft owns MULTIPLE runs (MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed two against one draft, plus a third orphan), Save Model adopts ONE, and the losing runs' prefixes are genuinely reclaimable. So the unit of the decision is the RUN, not the draft. Filter on the run: a run with modelId set has been adopted and its prefix is off limits, whatever its draft's status says. That also survives a future feature that adopts a second run from the same draft, which a draft-level guard would not.

T01 must additionally exclude SAVED from both windows, for the plain reason that a SAVED draft is not abandoned work — it is the provenance record of a model that exists.

VERIFY BY DELETION, NOT BY EXCLUSION: assert the adopted object is still readable AFTER a sweep that reclaimed its siblings in the same tick. A test that only proves the sweep skipped the draft cannot tell a working run-level guard from a sweep that happened to find nothing eligible.
tasks.note:
Completed 2026-08-31, as a per-run FILTER inside T01/T02 rather than a separate mechanism — no draft-level 'has an adopted run' skip exists, deliberately: that shape would make this task's own verify-by-deletion instruction impossible to satisfy (nothing would be left to prove survives). planReclaim() in the eligibility module: runIds.filter(r => r.modelId === null) drives the reclaim, and if EVERY run is adopted the reclaim shape is {subtree:false, runIds:[]} — nothing named, nothing deleted, while the draft can still be marked ABANDONED. SAVED excluded from both windows per this task's own instruction (T01's candidate query only ever selects ACTIVE/ABANDONED).

DELETION-SIDE PROOF, PER THIS TASK'S OWN DEMAND: test_object_store.py's test_reclaim_one_draft_run_leaves_its_sibling_run_readable writes two real run prefixes under one draft in live MinIO, reclaims ONE by {draft_id, run_id}, and asserts deleted>0 AND the sibling is still store.exists()-true afterward — the survival proof a mocked Nest spec cannot make. Backend-side: model-draft-cleanup.admin.service.spec.ts asserts an adopted run's id never appears in any postToPython call the same tick reclaims its sibling.

CURRENTLY UNSATISFIABLE BY REAL DATA, STATED PLAINLY: 0 ModelTrainingRun rows have modelId set anywhere in this dataset (adoption is MODEL-FLOW-007-T10, unbuilt) — this session's live sweep run therefore exercised the subtree branch throughout, not the per-run branch. The mechanism and its test coverage exist; a live end-to-end proof against a real adopted run does not yet, and cannot until -007 ships. This must land before -007, not after.

acceptance_criteria: A run that Save Model adopted is never reclaimed, and its object prefix survives a sweep that reclaims its unadopted siblings in the same tick. MECHANISM BUILT AND TESTED (unit + a live-MinIO deletion-side proof against a synthetic pair), NOT YET PROVED AGAINST A REAL ADOPTED ROW — 0 runs in this dataset have modelId set, because Save Model's adoption write (MODEL-FLOW-007-T10) does not exist yet. Ship this before -007, not after.
An ACTIVE ModelDraft with no runs becomes eligible after the short window and is reclaimed with no operator action. LIVE-VERIFIED (V01).
An ACTIVE ModelDraft owning runs is not reclaimed on the short window. LIVE-VERIFIED (V02).

A TRAINED draft is never reclaimed by either window. Verified by construction (the candidate query never selects TRAINED at all) plus unit tests; not separately live-walked since no TRAINED draft was a candidate to attempt reclaiming in this pass.
Reclaiming a draft also releases its runs' object prefixes. LIVE-VERIFIED (V03).
A RUNNING run whose container no longer exists reaches a terminal status at boot rather than staying RUNNING forever. LIVE-VERIFIED (V04).

The sweep runs without any HTTP call, and disabling it via env leaves any admin path working unchanged. Verified: onModuleInit's own log line at boot confirms the setInterval path is independent of any request; the admin route is registered and mapped in the same boot regardless of the interval; the <=0-disables branch has its own unit test, mirroring DS-LAKE-014's identical, already-shipped guarantee.

features.title: Run Parameter Recall Panel with Apply
features.description: After a run reaches a terminal state, list everything that produced that result in the right-hand column beneath Algorithm Insights: algorithm, every hyperparameter and its value, target, train/test split, seed, loss function, image digest, feature spec, plus the resulting metrics including RMSE. An Apply button loads those settings back into the Training Config form, where they can be edited before the next run.
findings: THE RUN ROW AND THE BROWSER DISAGREE THE MOMENT ANYTHING IS EDITED. An engineer comparing runs today has no record of what distinguished them — the run row holds the spec, the wizard holds a mutable draft, and useModelDraftSync's 600ms debounced PATCH means even the server draft is not reliably current. Rendering the DRAFT's values beside a finished run's metrics would read as provenance while being a live form. That is why T01 is task one and why acceptance criterion 1 is about the data SOURCE, not the layout.

LOSS FUNCTION IS ONE QUESTION, NOT TWO -- SUPERSEDES the earlier framing. T01's audit confirms the trainer never reads a loss field: images/trainer/train.py has zero occurrences of loss/objective/criterion. It is not that most algorithms can't consume it -- NONE of them receive it. The client never sends it, CreateTrainingRunSchema is .strict() so it would be rejected if it tried, and no run or draft column exists to hold it. It stops at the saved Model.data.config blob (ModelConfigSchema.lossFunction, model.authorized.dto.ts:72) and never enters the training path. The per-estimator objective analysis in the old framing (LinearRegression/Ridge take no loss param, MLPRegressor is fixed to squared error, etc.) is correct as sklearn trivia but moot here -- there is no case where a loss value reaches an estimator that can't use it, because no loss value reaches any estimator.

THE TRAINER DOES NOT SWALLOW VIA A KWARGS SPLAT -- CORRECTED MECHANISM. build_model (train.py:230-376) has no **hyperparameters splat anywhere; every branch is an explicit, named hyperparameters.get(key, default) call per constructor kwarg. An unrecognized key is silently ignored not because the trainer catches and drops it, but because nothing ever reads it. This makes 'sent but not consumed' a FIXED, enumerable key set per algorithm (verified key-for-key against lib/training-config.ts's HYPERPARAMS catalog: they agree exactly for all ten runnable algorithms), not a runtime introspection question. For UI-launched runs today this case is empty -- every hyperparameter the form can send is a key some branch of build_model reads. The label still ships, pinned by a static source test, because legacy rows, fine-tuning-job rows, and future catalog drift are real cases. seed is a separate, real instance of this same class: it is generated and recorded on EVERY run but is only forwarded as random_state to 6 of the 10 estimators (not ridge/ols/svm/pls) -- the panel must label it per-algorithm the same way.

SPLIT RATIO HAS THREE HOMES AND TWO UNITS. MODEL-FLOW-006 recorded it live: Model.data.config.trainTestSplit is a PERCENTAGE (70/80/85 observed), ModelDraft.splitRatio is a FRACTION, ModelTrainingRun.splitSpec.ratio is a FRACTION. This panel reads a run and writes a draft, so it crosses that boundary in both directions.

SPLIT RATIO HAS A FOURTH HOME. T01 found the same fraction/percentage split MODEL-FLOW-006 recorded, plus one more: request body trainTestSplit (fraction, model-run.authorized.dto.ts:68) -> run.splitSpec.ratio (fraction) -> ModelDraft.splitRatio (fraction) -> ModelConfigSchema.trainTestSplit on the SAVED Model (PERCENTAGE, 50-95, model.authorized.dto.ts:73-82). This panel reads the run (fraction) and Apply writes the draft (fraction); the Step 3 control itself is a percentage. Convert once at the client boundary, per MODEL-FLOW-002-T09's rule -- do not touch the fourth home, that's MODEL-FLOW-007's unification.

tasks.title: RunParamsPanel — read-only list under Algorithm Insights
tasks.detail: No new persistence: the run row IS the record, the same finding that made MODEL-FLOW-004-T05 a read task rather than a write task. ModelDraft gains no column. Honest empty states, not blanks: no run yet, still training, FAILED or CANCELED with the reason named, and a legacy run whose hyperparameters were never recorded. MODEL-FLOW-004 added four such states for the same column of the same wizard — reuse that vocabulary rather than inventing a second one.
tasks.note: Completed 2026-08-27. RunParamsPanel (training-config/run-params-panel.tsx), mounted under RuntimeEstimate in Step 3's right column. useDraftRuns (hooks/model/use-draft-runs.ts, mirrors useModelDrafts' plain-local-state shape) supplies the run picker; deliberately has NO Loss function row — see the component's own doc comment: the run row has no such column (T01), so rendering one would mean reading mpLossFunctionAtom next to run-sourced fields, the exact provenance-theatre mixing acceptance criterion 1 forbids. CORRECTED 2026-08-27, caught before commit: the first pass called useDraftRuns' refetch nowhere, so the panel fetched once on mount (getting []) and never again — Phase3TrainingConfig stays mounted through the whole training cycle (the poll loop lives in the same component), so nothing else remounts the panel when a run finishes. Fixed by watching mpTrainStateAtom.status and calling refetch() on every transition, not just 'done' — that also makes the QUEUED/RUNNING Apply-disabled branch reachable for a run just started, which it wasn't before. Also added: a target/dataset-mismatch note (a run outlives the dataset selection that produced it — Step 2 can change the draft's dataset after a run trained against a different one; Apply still writes the target, Start Training would 400 on it, so the panel names the mismatch rather than either silently omitting the write or leaving the failure unexplained). Both caught by an advisor pass before declaring done, both covered by new tests in run-params-panel.test.tsx (9/9).

tasks.title: Recheck lossFunction end to end, and show what is TRUE of it per algorithm
tasks.detail:
Two traces, not one. (a) Does it reach the container: follow the client atom through CreateTrainingRunSchema to the run row to /claim. (b) Does the estimator consume it: see this feature's second finding for why most of the catalogue cannot.

Because the trainer swallows unknown kwargs silently, a loss value that lands nowhere is invisible. The panel must therefore show one of three states per run — used by the estimator / sent but not consumed by this estimator / not sent — and must not print a bare 'MSE' that a reader will take for the objective that was optimised.

If (b) comes back 'not consumed for most algorithms', that is a real finding about the shipped UI and belongs in this ledger's findings, not buried in a panel label. Whether to then hide, disable or annotate the Loss function control in Step 3 is a product decision — recorded here, not taken here.

Also recheck the client inconsistency MODEL-FLOW-006 recorded but did not fix: resetWizardAtom defaults lossFunction to 'mse' while resetPipeline defaults it to 'rmse'. Whichever is right, two reset writers disagreeing means the displayed value depends on how the wizard was entered.
tasks.note: DECIDED 2026-08-27 (user): keep the Loss function control, annotate honestly rather than remove or disable. It continues to write only Model.data.config (ModelConfigSchema.lossFunction) on Save Model; the Step 3 control gains a note that it records intent on the saved model and is not sent to the trainer. Drop cross_entropy from LOSS_OPTIONS -- this is a regression-only pipeline (build_model has no classifier branch). The panel shows the run's lossFunction state as 'not sent to training' rather than a bare value, per T01's finding-2 rewrite. Also fixes the resetPipeline vs resetWizardAtom/atom-default divergence ('rmse' vs 'mse') found during this audit -- resetPipeline fires on every workspace/plant change, so it was silently flipping the displayed loss function on a workspace switch. Implemented 2026-08-27: LOSS_OPTIONS (lib/training-config.ts) dropped cross_entropy and gained a doc comment stating the audited fact; core-config.tsx's Loss function control gained a one-line note ('Recorded on the saved model. Not sent to the trainer...'); resetPipeline's setLossFunctionAtom('rmse') corrected to 'mse', matching mpLossFunctionAtom's own default and resetWizardAtom. The panel itself carries no Loss-function row at all — see T04's note for why that is correct, not an omission.

tasks.title: Apply writes through RAW atom setters, never useModelPipelineNav
tasks.detail: THE TRAP, WITH PRECEDENT: useModelPipelineNav.setAlgorithm OVERWRITES hyperparameters with that algorithm's defaults and relocks highestUnlocked, and every setter in that hook calls resetTraining(). MODEL-FLOW-010-T08 hit this exact wall building draft resume; its note states the resolution (hydrate with raw setters) and its fixture deliberately stores a hyperparameter set that is NOT the algorithm's defaults so that a later refactor routing through the nav hook fails loudly instead of silently applying defaults. Copy that fixture discipline here — an Apply routed through the nav hook typechecks, renders, and applies the wrong values.
tasks.note: Completed 2026-08-27. use-apply-run-params.ts writes ONLY raw atom setters imported from store/model-pipeline.ts — no import of useModelPipelineNav. Pinned by V01's fixture (ridge alpha:0.037, not ridge's 1.0 default): use-apply-run-params.test.tsx asserts the atom holds 0.037 after Apply, which would fail if Apply were routed through setAlgorithm.

tasks.title: Decide and implement Apply's relock semantics
tasks.detail: Apply changes the training configuration, so the evaluation on screen no longer corresponds to it. Two defensible options; the wrong outcome is picking neither. (a) Relock to Training Config, consistent with the nine relock sites MODEL-FLOW-010-T02 already maintains for every other training-config edit. (b) Keep the evaluation visible behind a banner stating it belongs to a previous run. Silently leaving Step 5 showing a stale run's charts beside freshly-applied parameters is the failure class this ledger keeps naming: it looks like success. Record the choice and the reason.
tasks.note: Completed 2026-08-27, per the decision recorded above: useApplyRunParams explicitly calls setTrainState({status:'idle', progress:0}) and setHighestUnlocked(prev => Math.min(prev, 3)) after every raw-atom write, replicating what resetTraining()/the nav setters' relock would have done. Tested: relocks 5 -> 3, and never RAISES a lower value (2 stays 2).

tasks.title: Cross-algorithm Apply must be refused or must switch the algorithm — never silently pass
tasks.detail: Applying ridge's hyperparameters into an SVR form produces no error anywhere: the client has no cross-check and the trainer accepts unknown kwargs silently. The run would train on SVR defaults while the form displays ridge's values. Apply must either switch the algorithm to the source run's — in which case T06's raw-setter rule is what stops the switch from wiping the very values being applied — or refuse and name the mismatch.
tasks.note: Completed 2026-08-27, per the decision recorded above: applyRun always sets mpAlgorithmsAtom = [run.algorithm] and mirrors mpAlgorithmAtom, plus forces both AutoML atoms false so showHyperparams reveals the applied values. Tested with a form pre-set to ['svm','xgboost'] applying a ridge run — atoms end at exactly ['ridge'].

tasks.title: Applied hyperparameters must satisfy the existing scalar constraint
tasks.detail: MODEL-FLOW-006 tightened PatchModelDraftSchema.hyperparameters from z.unknown() to the same HyperparametersSchema scalar constraint the run path enforces. A legacy run may hold a value that schema now refuses, so Apply's PATCH would 400 — and useModelDraftSync's debounced writer swallows failures, so the user would go on configuring against a draft that silently stopped accepting updates. That is the same silent-failure mechanism MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's third recorded gap describes for a SAVED draft. Validate before applying and state what was dropped.
tasks.note: NO-OP ON THE WIRE, explicit per this task's own instruction. T01 traced both write paths that can put hyperparameters on a run row: CreateTrainingRunSchema.hyperparameters (UI path) and CreateFineTuningJobSchema.hyperparameterSets: z.array(HyperparametersSchema) (job path, model-fine-tuning.authorized.dto.ts:27) -- both the SAME HyperparametersSchema scalar constraint PatchModelDraftSchema.hyperparameters already enforces. runDtoFor (model-fine-tuning.authorized.service.ts:52-68) hand-builds the run DTO from an already-validated set, not from unchecked input. A legacy run predating MODEL-FLOW-006's tightening could in principle still hold a non-scalar value, so the client-side Apply path (toApplyPatch in lib/run-params.ts) filters defensively and states what it dropped -- but no backend change is needed to prevent the PATCH from 400ing on data this system itself wrote. Client-side belt-and-suspenders added 2026-08-27: lib/run-params.ts's toApplyPatch scalar-filters the run's hyperparameters before they reach setHyperparameters, returning `dropped` for the panel to name — covers a legacy row this system itself never wrote, since T01 confirmed both write paths already prevent one.

tasks.title: splitRatio: convert once, at the client boundary
tasks.detail: The panel displays what the run used (fraction, from splitSpec.ratio) and Apply writes the draft (fraction) while the Step 3 control is a percentage. Convert at the client boundary, the convention MODEL-FLOW-002-T09 established and MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's hydration follows (0.8 -> 80). Unifying the unit itself is MODEL-FLOW-007's job, once Save Model can derive it from the adopted run's own splitSpec instead of trusting the browser — do not attempt it here.
tasks.note: Completed 2026-08-27. lib/run-params.ts's splitPercentFromRun(splitSpec) = Math.round(ratio * 100), the single conversion point Apply and the panel's display both call — never touches ModelConfigSchema.trainTestSplit's percentage (that's MODEL-FLOW-007's unification, per this feature's rewritten finding 4).

tasks.title: Apply from inside a candidate set
tasks.detail: Coupling with MODEL-FLOW-013: once candidate jobs exist, most Apply clicks will land on a run belonging to a job rather than a standalone run. Decide and record: refuse while the job is still QUEUED or RUNNING, since a config edit mid-sweep has no coherent meaning; and on a terminated job treat Apply as seeding a NEW configuration not attached to the old job. The one-live-job-per-draft index means a second job cannot start until the first terminates anyway, so the refusal is consistent with the rest of the system rather than a special case.
tasks.note: DECIDED 2026-08-27: refuse Apply while the source run itself is QUEUED/RUNNING -- run.status alone is sufficient data for this, already on every row this panel reads. The job-level rule (refuse mid-sweep, treat post-terminal Apply as seeding a new unattached configuration) is DEFERRED, not built: there is no stable job-status read to bind to until MODEL-FLOW-013-T03 generalizes ModelFineTuningJob into a candidate job. Recorded here so it isn't silently dropped when 013 lands. Implemented 2026-08-27: RunParamsPanel disables Apply whenever run.status is QUEUED or RUNNING ('Available once this run finishes.'), reading only the selected run's own status — no job fetch.

acceptance_criteria: Every value in the panel comes from the run row. No value is read from the current draft or from a wizard atom — proven by a test, not by inspection.
Every hyperparameter the container actually received is shown; anything sent but not consumed by the estimator is labelled as such rather than displayed as though it took effect.
Apply loads the settings into the form, they remain editable, and the edited values are what the next run uses.
Apply never replaces hyperparameters with the algorithm's defaults.
Applying a run from a different algorithm cannot produce a run that silently trains on defaults.
No Model row is created, and ModelDraft gains no column.
The panel behaves honestly for a draft with no run, a run in flight, a failed run, and a legacy run with no recorded hyperparameters.

features.title: Step 4 — Model Selection: compare candidate runs before Evaluation
features.description: A step between Training Configuration and Evaluation that shows each candidate model's result — a per-epoch loss curve where the algorithm has iterations, a train-vs-test loss value chart where it does not — and lets the user choose which model carries forward to Evaluation and Save Model. The step exists in shipped code as of 2026-08-27; this feature is what it takes to make it real and to make this ledger stop describing a five-step flow.
userDecisions: STEP COUNT (resolved 2026-08-27): six steps, and the shipped UI already has them — Select Dataset -> Dataset Review -> Training Config -> Model Selection -> Evaluation -> Save Model. This file is the stale artefact, not the product. T01 owns the reconcile.

LOSS VISUALISATION (resolved 2026-08-27): a per-epoch curve where the estimator genuinely iterates; a loss-function VALUE chart (train vs test, paired marks) for everything else. Two modes, never one faked into the other.

CANDIDATE ORCHESTRATION (resolved 2026-08-27): generalize ModelFineTuningJob to carry N algorithms rather than build a third orchestrator table. This is the direct build-out of MODEL-FLOW-003-T10's own blocked_reason.
ONE LIVE JOB PER DRAFT (resolved 2026-08-27): the partial unique index keeps its (draftId) key, not (draftId, kind). Sweep and tune cannot overlap — which is what forces T11.

SELECTION OVERRIDE (resolved 2026-08-27): the user may override the metric's winner, and the override is recorded in its own field. bestRunId is NOT overwritten — see T08 for why that matters beyond bookkeeping.
findings: THE STEP IS ALREADY IN THE WIZARD; THIS LEDGER IS THE THING THAT IS WRONG. MODEL-FLOW-010-T01 did a four-to-five reconcile on 2026-08-20 and verified it by grepping for 'four-step' — a method that cannot detect a sixth step arriving later, which is why the same drift recurred within a week. T01 enumerates every step-numbered assertion against MP_TOTAL_STEPS and STEP_LABELS instead of grepping for a number. Step 1's NAME is stale too: the contract says 'Model Setup', the product says 'Select Dataset', and no number-based check would ever surface that.

N CANDIDATES DO NOT EXIST YET. MODEL-FLOW-003-T10 enforces exactly one target and one algorithm per run and its client-side AutoML refusal is still in place. The Find Best Model and Find Best Parameters toggles have no training-container counterpart. So a comparison step ships today with at most one thing to compare — T03 is what supplies the rest, and until it lands this step is a frame around a single row.

THERE IS NO TRAIN-SIDE LOSS ANYWHERE IN THE SYSTEM. Observed metrics are {r2, mae, rmse, test_rows, train_rows, feature_count} — test split only. holdoutMetrics is null on every run observed, cause confirmed in MODEL-FLOW-004 (the holdout SOURCE object is absent; train.py's own comment documents this as the common case, not a bug). So 'loss vs validation loss' has no data behind it today in either mode, which makes T04 a prerequisite rather than a refinement.

MOST OF THE CATALOGUE HAS NO ITERATIONS TO PLOT. OLS and Ridge are closed-form; PLS, GRP, SVR and RandomForest have no loss trajectory. For those a curve cannot be produced — not 'has not been produced yet'. Drawing a line between a train point and a test point would imply a trajectory that does not exist and would be indistinguishable from a real curve to a reader, which is the MODEL-FLOW-000-T02 failure shape: it looks like success. The gap between two paired marks is what an engineer actually reads off a learning curve, and it survives the honest rendering.

EVEN WHERE A CURVE IS POSSIBLE, THE VALIDATION SERIES IS NOT. train.py passes no eval_set, so LightGBM and XGBoost produce no validation history and MLPRegressor's loss_curve_ is training-only. Mode A therefore needs a fit-time change, not just a new read endpoint. And the second series is the TEST split, not a holdout — label it that way, or repeat the misnomer MODEL-FLOW-004 had to rename ('Validation residual diagnostics' -> 'Test-split residual diagnostics') one feature after it was fixed.

THE STEP HOLDS ONE PIECE OF SERVER STATE AND ONLY ONE: selectedRunId on the job. Stated up front the way MODEL-FLOW-010's third finding was, so the step is not handed a column by reflex. ModelDraft gains nothing.

tasks.title: Generalize ModelFineTuningJob into a candidate job that varies algorithm as well as hyperparameters
tasks.detail:
hyperparameterSets becomes candidates, an ordered array of {algorithm, hyperparameters}; the job's own algorithm field moves down into each element. targetY, goldArtifactId and trainTestSplit STAY on the job — they are what makes the candidates comparable at all, and varying them would make the comparison meaningless. Rename the entity and ModelTrainingRun.fineTuningJobId, and backfill existing jobs with kind = 'HYPERPARAMETER_SEARCH'.

WHY GENERALIZE RATHER THAN ADD: MODEL-FLOW-005 already built this orchestrator and live-verified it with three real hyperparameter searches, catching a real currentRunId bug in the process. An algorithm sweep is the same loop with a different thing varying per element. A second table would duplicate advanceJobForRun's compare-and-swap, its idempotency, its failure semantics and its reconcile-on-read path — four things that took a live session to get right once.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: the compare-and-swap idempotency; both call sites (the container webhook as a best-effort nudge that can never fail the response, since a training container has no way to retry a 500; and getJobService reconciling on read); fail-whole-job semantics with the set index named; and retry-the-failed-set behaviour. The existing 9-test spec must pass unmodified wherever behaviour is unchanged — a test that needed editing to keep passing is the signal that behaviour moved.

RMSE remains the selection metric and this task does not reopen it: comparing RMSE across algorithms on one artifact, target and split is sound, and is the same reason MODEL-FLOW-005 chose it over R² after a real run scored r2 = -1,110,858 while its rmse stayed readable.

The partial unique index keeps its (draftId) key. One live job per draft.
tasks.note: Completed 2026-08-28. Hand-written migration (20260827120000_model_flow_013_candidate_job/migration.sql, following the two existing hand-added-SQL precedents in this schema) rather than `prisma migrate dev`-generated: existing rows' hyperparameterSets had no embedded algorithm, so this is a data migration (add nullable -> backfill via jsonb_agg(elem || jsonb_build_object('algorithm', algorithm)) -> tighten NOT NULL -> drop the old columns -> rename table/enum/FK/indexes -> recreate the partial unique index under its new name). Did NOT run that reset. Applied this migration instead via `prisma db execute --file`, which bypasses migration-state bookkeeping entirely — `_prisma_migrations` was NOT updated for this migration, so a future clean `prisma migrate dev` run will need to reconcile both this gap and the pre-existing droppedBadRows one together. tasks.title: Write a loss history artifact for the estimators that have one, and pass an eval_set so the validation series exists
tasks.detail:
MLPRegressor's loss_curve_; LightGBM and XGBoost's evals_result_, which requires passing eval_set at fit time and is currently not passed, so there is no second series to read; HistGradientBoosting's train_score_ and validation_score_. Write loss_history.json under drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/, alongside the keys already produced there.

Bound it: a run with many thousands of iterations must not ship an unbounded array. Refuse or aggregate BY NAME, the discipline MODEL-FLOW-004 applied with MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS rather than silently sampling — and record the deferred design in the schema's own comment for whoever hits the cap first, as that feature did. An estimator with no iterations writes no artifact and no placeholder.
tasks.note: Completed 2026-08-28. New extract_loss_history(algorithm, model) in train.py, called right after .fit(). eval_set added to the lightgbm/xgboost .fit() calls ONLY (no early_stopping_rounds anywhere, so this never changes when training stops or what the fitted model is); xgboost's eval_metric moved to the CONSTRUCTOR (build_model) since its sklearn API deprecates passing it to .fit(). loss_history.json written only when a series was extracted; registered in the three places the existing four run-artifact filenames are (train.py's outputs dict, Python's _ALLOWED_RUN_UPLOADS via new LOSS_HISTORY_FILENAME constant in object_store.py, TS RUN_UPLOAD_FILENAMES in artifact-keys.ts — RunUploadFilenameEnum/RunUploadUrlsSchema derive from that array automatically, no separate edit needed). Backend: ModelTrainingRun.lossHistoryKey (added in T03's migration), written in complete() via the same keyIf('loss_history.json') pattern the other four keys already use. LIVE-VERIFIED against the pinned library versions (scikit-learn 1.5.2, lightgbm 4.5.0, xgboost 2.1.2) with real fits on synthetic data across all 10 runnable algorithms, not just the fake-object unit tests — this caught a real bug before it shipped: HistGradientBoostingRegressor.train_score_ and validation_score_ are NOT absent when early_stopping resolves False (the unconfigured 'auto' default for any dataset at or under 10,000 rows — the common case in this trainer's domain, see GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS) — they are EMPTY ARRAYS, always present as attributes. The first implementation checked hasattr()/is None and would have shipped a technically-present-but-empty series, which is worse than no artifact — it looks like a real (empty) curve rather than an honest 'no data' state. Fixed to check len()==0. Net real-world effect: hist_gradient_boosting has NO loss history for most datasets in this system today and correctly falls to mode B (T05a/T07) — an accurate finding about this trainer, not a bug to route around. Confirmed via the same live-fit script: ols/ridge/pls/grp/svm/random_forest -> None; mlp -> train-only, metric=loss; hist_gradient_boosting -> None (small dataset, as expected); lightgbm/xgboost -> train+validation, metric=rmse, lengths matching n_estimators. images/trainer/test_train.py: 12/12 (7 new for extract_loss_history, including a dedicated regression test for the exact bug found). MAX_LOSS_HISTORY_POINTS=5000, soft-skip (log + omit, never fails the run) when exceeded, same discipline as apps/python's MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS. apps/python/tests/: 772 passed, 74 skipped (pre-existing skip set, unaffected). pnpm --filter=backend check-types/jest: unchanged from T03 (5 pre-existing unrelated errors, 30/31 with the same pre-existing RunTokenGuard DI gap).

tasks.title: Comparison chart and selection UI, with two honest render modes
tasks.detail:
One row per candidate showing its algorithm, hyperparameters and metrics, plus the chart. Mode A: train and validation series over iterations, the second series labelled TEST SPLIT because that is what it is. Mode B: the loss value as PAIRED MARKS, train beside test — never a two-point line, for the reason this feature's fourth finding states.

NO FABRICATED SERIES, EVER. MODEL-FLOW-004 deleted seededNoise, comparePoints and compareFit from this same wizard for exactly this reason, and disabled its 'Compare with...' control rather than let it invent a series to fill the space. A candidate with no history shows mode B and says why; a FAILED candidate shows its reason and stays in the list rather than disappearing.

tasks.title: Record the user's choice in selectedRunId; leave bestRunId alone
tasks.detail:
Add ModelCandidateJob.selectedRunId, nullable, where null means 'accept the metric's answer'. bestRunId becomes immutable once the job terminates. One resolver returns selectedRunId ?? bestRunId, and Evaluation, Save Model and the ModelDraft.currentRunId write all read through it.

WHY NOT JUST OVERWRITE bestRunId: it is the record of what the metric chose, so overwriting destroys the only evidence that a human chose differently — the fact an audit would actually want. It also reopens a bug MODEL-FLOW-005 closed live: before that fix, a child run finishing mid-search set ModelDraft.currentRunId to itself rather than leaving it for the eventual winner, and Step Evaluation showed that intermediate run for the whole search's duration. The fix works by narrowing the writers of that field to exactly one, advanceJobForRun's completion branch. A user-selection writer would be a third, racing the same field.

THE INVARIANT: ModelDraft.currentRunId keeps ONE writer. Selection writes selectedRunId; the resolver is a read. Any implementation that ends up with a second writer to currentRunId has not implemented this task, whatever it returns.

Refuse a selection while the job is not terminal, and refuse a runId that is not a candidate of this job or did not SUCCEED. A client-only selection is not an option: Save Model runs server-side and adopts by pointer, so a browser-held choice would fall back to bestRunId at the one moment it matters — the same reason decisions.draft_persistence rejected a client-only draft.

tasks.title: Find Best Model and Find Best Parameters are two PHASES of one job, not two jobs
tasks.detail:
Forced by the (draftId)-scoped one-live-job index together with the shipped UI's own copy: 'Find Best Parameters — Hyperparameter-tune the best model. Requires Find Best Model.' Two concurrent jobs are impossible under that index, so a sweep-then-tune request is ONE job with an algorithm phase followed by a hyperparameter phase over the phase-1 winner. advanceJobForRun's compare-and-swap already sequences runs within a job; extending it to advance a PHASE when a phase's candidates are exhausted is the same mechanism one level up.

Scoped as its own task rather than folded into T03 because building the sweep first and discovering the phase requirement afterwards would mean reopening the job entity a second time — the cost this ledger has already paid twice, on ModelTrainingRun's owner column and on ModelConfigSchema.

features.title: Step 3 — Train/Test Split Distribution Panel, and an honest seed control
features.description: Two additions to Training Configuration, both about seeing what a split actually does before paying for a fit. (1) A per-tag box plot comparing the train side against the test side of the chronological split the run will really make, with tag selection, served by one new endpoint that reads the artifact once and returns both sides. (2) The estimator seed, currently server-generated and invisible, exposed as an optional field with copy that states what it does and does not control.
userDecisions: SPLIT-STATS SHAPE (resolved): option (b) — ONE new endpoint returning both sides from a single read, not two /boxplot calls with start_time/end_time. Two calls would open the artifact twice for one comparison, and would put the cut-point derivation in the CLIENT, which is where it is least able to be right (see finding 1).

CUT POINT IS NOT A SEPARATE READ (resolved): the client sends split_ratio; the server derives the cut internally. No 'tell me the cut timestamp' endpoint — a client that had to ask, then ask again for each side, is the two-call design already rejected.

TAG SCOPE (resolved): every tag, with selection — not target-only. Covariate shift on a feature is as real a finding as a shifted target, and the selection is what keeps 20 tags x 2 sides from being 40 unreadable boxes.

SIDECAR (resolved, with a correction the original ask could not have known): a sidecar is wanted, but it CANNOT be written ahead of Step 3 — splitRatio is what the user is adjusting there, so anything frozen at GOLD/FINAL commit time would be stale the moment the slider moves. Resolved as two things that are not duplicates: computed LIVE for the panel (T04), and frozen into a sidecar AT RUN CREATION (T06), which records what the user was actually looking at when they pressed Start Training.
SEED (resolved): optional, undefined means the server's own default. See finding 4 for why this is the ESTIMATOR seed and why a split seed is not being added.
findings: THE CUT IS ON LABELLED ROWS, NOT ON ROWS — AND GETTING THIS WRONG WOULD BE INVISIBLE. train.py drops every non-Good TARGET row BEFORE calling chronological_split, so the real boundary is at `int(len(labelled) * ratio)`, not `int(len(frame) * ratio)`. For this system's own worst case — a lab target sampled daily against a 1-minute PI grid, the exact case MODEL-FLOW-000-T02 exists for — those two cut timestamps are months apart. An endpoint that cuts on total row count would render two box plots of a split the trainer never makes, and every number in them would look entirely plausible. This is the MODEL-FLOW-000-T02 failure shape in a new place: it looks like success. T01 must confirm the rule against train.py directly rather than trusting this finding.

THE EXISTING /boxplot IS ALREADY WRONG FOR THIS QUESTION, AND WRONG FOR EVERY OTHER CALLER TOO. boxplot_service.py filters on start_time (line ~157) and THEN calls `frame.head(request.sample_rows)` (line ~161). On a time-ordered frame, head() of a filtered window is that window's EARLIEST contiguous period — so a test-side box would summarise the first sample_rows of the test period, not the test period. Worse for this feature's purpose: the train-side box would summarise the earliest rows of train, so the two boxes being compared are two adjacent early windows, not two sides of a split. This is a PRE-EXISTING defect affecting the Step 3.1 boxplot tab as well, not something this feature introduces — recorded here because this feature is what surfaces it, and T02 is what fixes it for both. T01 RE-AUDIT (2026-09-01): the SAME five-line filter-then-head() shape exists in histogram_service.py:140, scatter_service.py:119 and correlation_matrix_service.py:94 — T02's fix is scoped to all four, not boxplot alone, so the Step 3.1 tabs stop disagreeing with each other and with this panel.

end_time DOES EXIST ON BoxplotRequest (CORRECTED 2026-09-01) — schemas/preprocess.py:1296 `end_time: Optional[str] = None`, consumed at boxplot_service.py:159-160. T01's re-audit found the original claim false; recorded here rather than silently fixed, since the option-(b) decision this finding was cited to support still stands on its own real grounds (one read, server derives the cut) and does not depend on end_time being absent.

random_state HAS NO SPLIT TO RANDOMISE, AND MUST NOT BE GIVEN ONE. chronological_split cuts by time and draws nothing at random; the field the request already carries is `seed`, which model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts generates via randomInt when omitted and which train.py forwards as random_state to 6 of the 10 estimators only (MODEL-FLOW-012's own T01 audit enumerated exactly which: hist_gradient_boosting, mlp, grp, random_forest, lightgbm, xgboost — NOT ridge/ols/svm/pls). So this task exposes an existing field, it does not add a concept. A SPLIT seed is deliberately not being added: a randomised split on time-series data lets training see rows from after the test period, which is leakage — the same class of defect assert_no_target_leakage and assert_no_window_leakage both exist to catch, arriving through the split rather than through a feature.

THE SEED CONTROL INHERITS MODEL-FLOW-012-T05's PROBLEM VERBATIM. That task established that Loss function ships a control whose value never reaches the trainer, and resolved it by annotating rather than removing. seed is the mirror image — it DOES reach the trainer, but only reaches the ESTIMATOR for 6 of 10 algorithms. The per-algorithm labelling MODEL-FLOW-012's RunParamsPanel already does (SEED_CONSUMING_ALGORITHMS, pinned by a live source guard against build_model) is the vocabulary to reuse here, not a second one.

THIS PANEL HAS NO SERVER STATE OF ITS OWN. It reads the dataset's committed artifact and a ratio the draft already holds. ModelDraft gains no column — stated up front the way MODEL-FLOW-010's third finding and MODEL-FLOW-013's sixth were, so it is not handed one by reflex. T06's sidecar is written at RUN creation and lives beside the run's own artifacts, not on the draft.

T01 AUDIT (2026-09-01): the preprocess router's `_run` (routers/preprocess.py:117-194) maps ValueError -> 422 and bare Exception -> 502 with an opaque message. There is no RuntimeError branch. Both refusals chronological_split raises in train.py ("leaves one side empty", <30 labelled rows) are RuntimeError there — ported verbatim they would surface as an opaque 502. /split-stats raises ValueError for both, per the convention every sibling service states on itself (boxplot_service.py:145-149).

T01 AUDIT (2026-09-01): sample_rows must never determine the cut. Chart services cap at 5,000 rows by default while chronological_split runs over the ENTIRE labelled frame — deriving the cut from a capped head would silently show the split of the first sample_rows, the exact plausible-but-meaningless failure train.py's own module docstring warns about. /split-stats cuts on the full labelled frame; sample_rows only bounds the per-tag box statistics computed on each side afterward.

T01 AUDIT (2026-09-01): T07's premise that SEED_CONSUMING_ALGORITHMS is "pinned by a live source guard against build_model" is FALSE. run-params.test.ts:108-120 hand-types the same six algorithms it asserts against — it never reads train.py. Worse, the lstm/gru assertion at run-params.test.ts:99-105 is a false pass: its regex now matches the LSTM_MAX_TRAIN_WINDOWS ceiling raise (train.py:722-730), not an unconditional one. train.py:738 already passes lstm/gru a seed (as `seed=seed`, not `random_state=`) and CONSUMED_HYPERPARAM_KEYS.lstm/gru = [] is stale against HYPERPARAMS.lstm/gru (training-config.ts:253-320). Correct count: 8 of 12 algorithms consume the seed, not 6 of 10. T07 builds a real live guard rather than reusing this one.
