tasks.title: Fix boxplot_service's head() sampling so a windowed box describes its window
tasks.detail:
PRE-EXISTING DEFECT, FIXED HERE BECAUSE THIS FEATURE SURFACED IT — not scope creep, and not deferred either: T03 cannot be correct while the primitive it mirrors is wrong, and the Step 3.1 boxplot tab is silently wrong today for the same reason.

Replace `frame.head(sample_rows)` with an evenly-spaced (systematic) sample over the whole frame under consideration. A box plot summarises a DISTRIBUTION; head() on time-ordered data samples one contiguous period, which is a different claim wearing the same shape. Keep the cap — the point is which rows the cap keeps, not whether there is one.

STATE THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE IN THIS LEDGER, do not slip it in: existing boxplot numbers for any artifact larger than sample_rows WILL move, and they will move toward being right. A reader comparing a screenshot from before this change to one after must be able to find out why.

Guard against the silent-no-op class this repo has hit before (DS-LAKE-016-T02's prefix bug reported success having deleted nothing): assert the sampled frame spans the window's full time range, not merely that it has the expected row count.

Field descriptions in schemas/preprocess.py and router descriptions in routers/preprocess.py updated to state the new sampling, not silently changed. 5 new tests in test_downsample.py assert the sampled frame's timestamp SPAN equals the source frame's (V02's own point: a row-count-only check would pass unchanged against the old head() behaviour). tasks.title: The panel: paired box plots per selected tag, with the cut stated
tasks.detail:
One paired box per selected tag — train beside test — with the resolved cut_timestamp and both labelled-row counts shown as text, not implied. A reader who cannot see WHERE the split fell cannot interpret the boxes.

Tag selection: reuse the existing compare-tags/selection vocabulary rather than inventing a third one. Default to the target alone — it is the one tag whose distribution shift directly explains a bad test score — and let the user add features.

HONEST STATES, reusing MODEL-FLOW-004's vocabulary (that feature added four such states to this same wizard column; a second set of words for the same conditions is how a UI starts contradicting itself): no dataset selected; no committed artifact; loading; a tag insufficient on one side only, labelled per side; and a ratio that leaves one side empty, which the API refuses and the panel explains.

DO NOT DRAW A CONNECTOR between the train box and the test box. Two sides of a split are two populations, not a trajectory — the same reasoning MODEL-FLOW-013's fourth finding gives for refusing to draw a line between a train point and a test point in mode B, and the gap between paired marks is what a reader actually reads off either chart.

tasks.title: Expose the estimator seed as optional, labelled per algorithm
tasks.detail:
The field already exists end to end (finding 4) — this adds a control, not a concept. Optional and nullable in client state: undefined must stay distinguishable from an explicit 42, because 'the user did not choose' and 'the user chose the default' are different facts when reproducing a run.

COPY MUST STATE BOTH HALVES. What it controls: the estimator's own randomness — bootstrap sampling, weight initialisation, feature subsampling. What it does NOT control: the train/test boundary, which is chronological, so the last N% of rows by time is always the test set. Omitting the second half invites exactly the reading this feature's own finding 4 refuses.

PER-ALGORITHM TRUTH, NOT A BLANKET LABEL: seed reaches random_state on 6 of 10 estimators. Reuse MODEL-FLOW-012's SEED_CONSUMING_ALGORITHMS and its live source guard against build_model rather than hand-copying a second list — that guard exists because a hand-copied table is how the client starts telling the user something the trainer stopped doing. tasks.title: Core Config commits on Apply, not on change
tasks.detail:
Today every Core Config control writes its atom on change, which /split-stats cannot follow: a ratio slider dragged from 70 to 85 would fire sixteen artifact reads for one decision, and debouncing only hides that rather than fixing it. Apply makes the commit explicit and gives the panel one thing to fetch against.

THE RELOCK QUESTION IS THE WHOLE DESIGN, NOT A DETAIL. use-model-pipeline-nav.ts holds NINE relock calls (setAlgorithm/setAlgorithms/setFindBestModel/setFindBestParams/setFetchTagOverride/setTargetVariable/setHyperparameter/setLossFunction/setTrainTestSplit), each dropping highestUnlocked to 3 the instant a control moves. Move the write to Apply and those nine either fire on a value the user has not committed, or stop firing at all — and the second failure leaves Evaluation showing a finished run's charts beside uncommitted parameters, which is precisely the state MODEL-FLOW-012-T07 refused to allow ('silently leaving Step 5 showing a stale run's charts beside freshly-applied parameters is the failure class this ledger keeps naming: it looks like success').

RESOLVE IT THE WAY -012-T07 ALREADY DID, do not invent a second mechanism: relock on APPLY, using the same setTrainState({status:'idle'}) + setHighestUnlocked(prev => Math.min(prev, 3)) pair useApplyRunParams performs — one relock writer, one meaning. Local draft edits before Apply relock nothing, because nothing downstream has changed yet.

DIRTY STATE MUST BE VISIBLE, not inferred: uncommitted edits are what makes Apply meaningful, and a user who cannot see that the form differs from what the panel and the next run will use is worse off than with onChange. Show it, and disable Start Training while dirty — starting a run against values the user can see on screen but has not committed is the same lie in the other direction.

CHECK BEFORE BUILDING, do not assume: whether MODEL-FLOW-012's own Apply (useApplyRunParams, which writes these same atoms from a finished run) now needs to write the local draft instead of the committed atoms, or whether it should keep writing committed state directly and count as its own Apply. Both are defensible; picking neither leaves two writers with different rules for the same fields.

features.title: Time-Series Cross-Validation, with holdout scoring as its own phase
features.description: Estimate a configuration's out-of-sample performance across k expanding time-ordered folds inside ONE run, so a run reports a spread rather than one number that may have landed on a lucky test window. A CV run produces fold metrics and NO predictions; scoring is a separate, user-triggered phase against the dataset's raw validation holdout.
userDecisions: SPLIT STAYS CHRONOLOGICAL (resolved, and now backed by measurement rather than argument — see finding 1). No shuffled k-fold, no split seed. TimeSeriesSplit only.

k FOLDS LIVE IN ONE RUN (resolved). Not k runs grouped as a candidate job: candidates are ALTERNATIVES to choose between, folds are SAMPLES to aggregate. Modelling folds as candidates would put five folds in front of the user with a Select button on each and would set bestRunId to whichever fold drew the easiest window — presenting sampling noise as a decision. It would also make CV and an algorithm sweep mutually exclusive under the one-live-job-per-draft index, the bind MODEL-FLOW-013-T11 had to resolve with phases.

EXPANDING WINDOW (resolved). Each fold trains on everything before its test window, which is how retraining actually happens in production — a plant never discards history. Rolling was considered and rejected on this dataset's own numbers: a fixed-width train window would leave each fold with even fewer distinct labelled observations than expanding already does (finding 2).

THE SAVED MODEL IS A REFIT ON ALL DATA (resolved, option b). Not one of the k fold models: fold 1 trains on a fraction of the data, so offering the folds as choices would mean offering k-1 options nobody should pick. The refit is fit number k+1.

A CV RUN WRITES NO predictions.parquet, AND THAT IS THE POINT (resolved, user's own framing): under CV there is no single held-out series to write. Fold metrics go to their own artifact; predictions come from a SEPARATE, user-triggered scoring phase against the validation holdout. This resolves the tension the refit decision would otherwise create — see finding 4.
findings: SHUFFLED SPLIT IS DISQUALIFIED BY THIS SYSTEM'S OWN DATA, NOT BY PRINCIPLE. Measured 2026-09-01 against a real predictions.parquet from run 61f9aa28 (the run MODEL-FLOW-004-V02 already cites for its -2.406723649677836 R²): 1,341 rows carry only NINETEEN distinct y_true values, with a median run of 67 consecutive identical rows and lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.9992. Copying the previous row's value scores R² = 0.9984 on that same window, against the real model's -2.4067. Under a shuffled split, adjacent rows land on opposite sides, so a nearest-neighbour lookup would score ~0.998 having learned nothing — the MODEL-FLOW-000-T02 failure shape (it looks like success) arriving through the split rather than through a feature, and undetectable by either existing guard: assert_no_target_leakage inspects target-derived FEATURES and assert_no_window_leakage inspects window spans; neither asks whether the cut itself was drawn at random. This also means MODEL-FLOW-014's own refusal to add a split seed was correct for a reason stronger than the one it recorded.

EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE IS THE DISTINCT LABEL COUNT, NOT THE ROW COUNT — AND THIS BREAKS NAIVE k. The same measurement: 19 distinct labelled values forward-filled across 1,341 rows on a 10-minute grid, roughly two lab readings per day over nine days. Five folds over that window gives each test fold about 1.8 days and THREE OR FOUR independent observations. An RMSE computed over four points is noise wearing a metric's clothes, and it would be indistinguishable from a real one in the UI. So n_splits must be capped by distinct labelled observations, not rows (T02) — and on a dataset like this the honest answer may be that CV cannot run at all, which the panel must say rather than executing five fits to produce five meaningless numbers.

THE REFIT HAS NO HELD-OUT SCORE OF ITS OWN, BY CONSTRUCTION. CV's fold metrics describe the CONFIGURATION; the saved model is a refit that has seen every row, so nothing in the CV output is a score for the artifact that gets deployed. Presenting a fold mean beside a refit model as though it were that model's performance is the same category error MODEL-FLOW-004 had to correct by RENAMING a heading ('Validation residual diagnostics' -> 'Test-split residual diagnostics') one feature after the confusion shipped. Naming the gap is not enough on its own — which is what makes the holdout phase below structural rather than a nicety.

THE HOLDOUT IS EXACTLY THE MISSING PIECE, AND IT ALREADY EXISTS. DS-LAKE-018 writes validate_data.parquet beside the BRONZE artifact — raw rows, split off before any cleaning, never seen by any fit. Three artifacts then each do one job and none of them overlaps: cv_folds.json says how much to trust the configuration; the refit model is what ships; the holdout score is that refit model's own honest number. Scoring against the holdout is also already built — replay_holdout_for_run (DS-LAKE-018-T05) and tryReplayHoldout (model-run.authorized.service.ts) — so this phase reuses a path rather than inventing one.

A LATENT BUG BECOMES LOAD-BEARING. MODEL-FLOW-004's own implementation note recorded, and verified by executing the guard, that tryReplayHoldout presigns .../validate_ready.parquet — a key is_committed_artifact_key REFUSES — and that it has simply never been reached, because every observed run failed one step earlier on a missing validate_data.parquet source object. Under this feature the holdout path stops being an optional extra that always silently skipped and becomes the ONLY way a CV run gets a prediction series. T08 fixes it BEFORE T07 depends on it, not after.

THE HOLDOUT IS OPTIONAL, SO THIS FEATURE HAS A PRECONDITION IT CANNOT SATISFY ALONE. holdoutMetrics is null on every run observed across MODEL-FLOW-004's and -010's own audits, cause confirmed: most datasets have no holdout, and train.py's own comment documents that as the common case rather than a bug. A CV run on a dataset with no holdout therefore reaches the scoring phase with nothing to score against. That must be stated at CONFIG time — before the user pays for k fits — not discovered at the end. DS-LAKE-018-T01 puts holdout selection at Step 2 of the DATASET wizard, so the fix is a precondition check here, not a new holdout mechanism.

splitSpec NEEDS A THIRD VARIANT AND THE PRECEDENT IS ONE WEEK OLD. RunCompleteSchema.splitSpec was widened to a discriminated union on `method` (chronological | chronological_windowed) by MODEL-FLOW-009-T04, after its .strict() literal shape would have 400'd a windowed run's own /complete call AFTER a successful fit — caught by inspection, one review short of shipping. A CV run carries k cut points, and train_rows/test_rows mean something different again on it. Add the variant in the same pass as the trainer change, not after.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-FLOW-016-T01, supersedes finding 5's cause, not its conclusion). Finding 5 states the presign refusal 'has simply never been reached, because every observed run failed one step earlier on a missing validate_data.parquet source object.' MEASURED against the live database and object store: that is false — it is the ACTIVE failure on every recent run. ModelTrainingRunLog carries "Holdout scoring skipped: '.../validate_ready.parquet' is not a committed artifact data key" on 10+ SUCCEEDED runs; validate_ready.parquet (74,040 bytes) exists in MinIO in every one of those run prefixes, beside its own manifest.json — the prepare_holdout_for_run WRITE leg succeeds. holdoutMetrics IS NOT NULL on 0 of 73 runs in the database, and holdout-bearing GOLD artifacts do exist (validationRowCount 878 and 1,153) — the cause is the presign refusal, not an absent holdout. Mechanism confirmed by reading: presignArtifact({source_key: targetKey}) (model-run.authorized.service.ts:197) calls is_committed_artifact_key, which requires '/artifacts/' in key — false for a drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/ key — raising ValueError, swallowed by the surrounding catch. T08 is therefore not preventive work: it is a live bug fix that unblocks holdout metrics for EVERY run in this system, not only CV runs. Finding 6's 'most datasets have no holdout' is not the operative cause on the runs actually observed and is corrected alongside this.

Confirmed by reading apps/python: this overstates the reuse the same way finding 5 overstated the write-leg's status. replay_holdout_for_run and prepare_holdout_for_run PREPARE the model-ready frame; model.predict exists only inside the trainer image (apps/python has no sklearn/joblib/lightgbm/torch installed). Pinned by a unit assertion (model-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts) so it cannot change silently, and confirmed live against the real ModelVersion row in V08.
openDecisions: DOES CV COMPOSE WITH AN ALGORITHM SWEEP? RESOLVED 2026-09-01: mutually exclusive, disabled with a stated reason — the same discipline lstm/gru, Find Best Parameters and Evaluation's 'Compare with…' control already follow in this wizard (one vocabulary, no new concept, no second budget constant). Superseded the original open framing (a cap in the TUNE_VARIANTS_PER_JOB mould was the alternative considered and rejected — it adds a second budget constant and a new silent-trim failure mode).

CAN A SCORING PHASE BE RE-RUN AGAINST A DIFFERENT HOLDOUT? A dataset's holdout is fixed at BRONZE (DS-LAKE-018), so today the answer is no by construction and the question is moot. It becomes live the moment a dataset can carry more than one holdout window — recorded so a future reader does not read T07's single-holdout assumption as an oversight.

CAN A CV RUN BE SAVED WITHOUT EVER BEING SCORED? RESOLVED 2026-09-02 by the user, before T12 was implemented (as that task's own OPEN DECISION required): YES, and Save Model WARNS. Scoring is draft-scoped — triggerScoringService calls assertDraftWritable, which refuses a SAVED draft — so saving is the point of no return: the model ships with fold metrics describing the CONFIGURATION and no held-out score of its own, permanently, with no way back. The alternative considered and rejected was silence plus a ledger note; the consequence is permanent AND undiscoverable afterward, which is what makes it worth a sentence on screen. A server-side REFUSAL was never on the table: it contradicts this feature's own framing that scoring is an optional pre-save Evaluation action. Implemented as a non-blocking notice in phase-6-deploy.tsx keyed off cvScoringPhaseOf(run) === 'awaiting-scoring', with a Back to Evaluation action; both Save buttons stay enabled, and config.crossValidation.holdoutScored records which way the user went.

tasks.title: Audit: the real cut rule, the distinct-label count, and what TimeSeriesSplit does to it
tasks.detail:
READ, DO NOT INFER — MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code, and -004/-005/-006/-012 each opened with an audit that changed their own scope.

Confirm from source: (a) that train.py applies the label mask BEFORE chronological_split, so a fold boundary must be computed over the labelled frame and not the row count — the same rule MODEL-FLOW-014-T01 is confirming for its own panel, and if the two features derive it separately they will drift; (b) how TimeSeriesSplit's own n_splits interacts with a frame whose rows are forward-filled from far fewer distinct observations, since sklearn counts rows and has no notion of an effective sample size; (c) whether MODEL-FLOW-009-T04's recorded window-count-vs-labelled-row-count divergence means a sequence algorithm needs a third fold rule here, or whether CV declares itself tabular-only for now and says so; (d) the current state of tryReplayHoldout and replay_holdout_for_run against finding 5.

Write the answers into this entry before any code. If (a) comes back cutting on total rows after all, findings 1 and 2 and the shape of T02 all change.
tasks.result: Confirmed against images/trainer/train.py directly, plus two real GOLD artifacts read live from MinIO (2026-09-01). (a) label_mask applied BEFORE chronological_split (train.py:805, step 8's cut is int(len(ordered)*ratio) over the LABELLED frame, line 188) — confirmed, matches finding 1; split_stats_service.py:152 already mirrors this exactly and test_split_stats_service.py pins the two labelled_mask implementations identical, so T02/T09 extend that existing mirror rather than adding a third copy. (b) MEASURED on artifact 66173c35 (S204FBP.lab, 8,350 rows, all labelled, 32 distinct y, lag-1 autocorr 0.99925, median identical run 288 rows) and artifact 798bec37 (15,441 rows, 97 distinct y): labelled_rows == row_count on both — the mask drops nothing here, so labelled_rows is useless as a sample-size proxy, confirming finding 2 on a second, independent dataset. sklearn's own TimeSeriesSplit test-fold distinct-label counts at k=3/5/10 recorded on both artifacts — this pair is the V02 cap-bites-both-ways proof, from real data. (c) CV is TABULAR ONLY, by existing precedent: split_stats_service.py's own docstring already declares this and refuses lstm/gru's window-count cut rule outright; CV extends that same endpoint so it inherits the scope — lstm/gru becomes a fourth disable-with-reason case in T10. (d) tryReplayHoldout's presign refusal IS real, but finding 5's stated cause is WRONG — see the CORRECTED finding below, established by executing the guard against live data, not by reading alone.

tasks.title: Cap n_splits by distinct labelled observations, and refuse rather than degrade
tasks.detail:
Per finding 2: rows are not observations here. Compute the distinct labelled count and derive the maximum admissible k as floor(distinct / MIN_LABELS_PER_FOLD).

MIN_LABELS_PER_FOLD IS A REAL CHOICE AND MUST BE MEASURED, NOT PICKED. The precedent is GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS and MODEL-FLOW-009-T04's LSTM_MAX_TRAIN_WINDOWS: both were set to the largest value ACTUALLY MEASURED with one further point shown safely beyond it, not extrapolated. Do the same — establish at what fold size the per-fold RMSE stops varying wildly between adjacent folds on real data, and record the measurement.

REFUSE, DO NOT SILENTLY REDUCE. A dataset admitting only one fold cannot be cross-validated, and running one fold under a CV label would produce a number indistinguishable from a real CV estimate — which is the whole failure class this ledger keeps naming. Say so at CONFIG time, before the user commits, so the check lands where the decision is made and not after k fits.

This figure belongs in MODEL-FLOW-014's /split-stats response, not a second endpoint: that endpoint already reads the artifact once and already derives the labelled count for its own cut. Adding a distinct-value count there is one more aggregate over a frame already in memory.
tasks.result: MIN_LABELS_PER_FOLD=10, MEASURED against scikit-learn 1.5.2 (the trainer's own pin) in a throwaway venv: fit Ridge (StandardScaler'd) across TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=k) for k=2..10 against the two real GOLD artifacts finding 1/T01 measured (32 and 97 distinct labelled values), recording per-fold RMSE, its coefficient of variation, and min-distinct-per-fold at every k. On BOTH artifacts, cv stays under 0.3 through k=3 and roughly doubles by k=4 — full table recorded in the constant's own comment in split_stats_service.py, matching GPR_MAX_TRAIN_ROWS/LSTM_MAX_TRAIN_WINDOWS's documentation discipline. The CONFOUND (k varies test size, train size, AND real regime-shift noise simultaneously) is stated explicitly in the comment, not hidden — 798bec37's k=4 fold has 20-24 distinct values yet its worst RMSE exceeds several sparser, higher-k folds elsewhere, proving this cap targets label thinness specifically and does not eliminate regime-shift noise (left to T11's per-fold table for a human to catch). Implemented as `max_admissible_k = distinct_labelled_values // MIN_LABELS_PER_FOLD` in split_stats_service.build_split_stats, landed in the EXISTING /split-stats endpoint (no second endpoint) alongside T09 in one pass. REFUSES, does not degrade: n_splits above the cap raises ValueError naming the reason, at config time. The fold-cut arithmetic itself (_expanding_fold_plan) was checked index-for-index against a REAL sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit for n in {8350, 15441, 1341, 100, 97, 33, 6} and k in 2..10: zero mismatches — apps/python carries no scikit-learn runtime dependency, so this arithmetic is hand-rolled and verified rather than imported. LIVE-VERIFIED against the real running dev server and both real artifacts (2026-09-01): n_splits=4 against the 32-distinct artifact returns 422 'n_splits=4 exceeds the admissible maximum of 3...'; n_splits=3 against the same artifact returns 200 with fold train_rows/test_rows/distinct EXACTLY matching the manual measurement table (2089/2087/8, 4176/2087/10, 6263/2087/8); n_splits=9 against the 97-distinct artifact returns 200 with 9 folds. This is V02's own 'cap bites both ways' proof, executed against real data, not synthetic. 15 unit tests added to test_split_stats_service.py, all passing, covering mutual exclusion, always-present distinct_labelled_values/max_admissible_k in both modes, no-box-statistics in CV mode, expanding-not-rolling folds, chronological-not-row-count cuts (V01's own CV analog), and both halves of V02's refusal/admission proof.

tasks.title: k expanding folds plus a refit, inside one run, in train.py
tasks.detail:
TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=k) over the LABELLED, time-ordered frame — never KFold, never shuffle=True, for the reason finding 1 measures rather than asserts. Prefer sklearn's own cross_validate over a hand-rolled loop; it returns per-fold train and test scores directly and is one less thing to get subtly wrong.

Then REFIT on the full labelled frame as fit k+1, and that is the model written to model.joblib. The k fold models are discarded — they exist to produce metrics, not artifacts.

Record train_rows PER FOLD, not just overall. Under an expanding window fold 1 trains on a fraction of what fold k does, so its metric is systematically worse for a reason that has nothing to do with the period it tested — a reader shown five RMSEs without five row counts will read a data-volume artefact as a regime change.

splitSpec gains a third discriminated-union variant (finding 7), carrying method, n_splits, and each fold's own cut timestamp and row counts. Do it in this same pass: MODEL-FLOW-009-T04's windowed variant was found one review short of 400ing a successful run's own /complete call, and the cost of that near-miss was only avoided because someone happened to look.
tasks.result: images/trainer/train.py restructured: is_cv = splitSpec.method == 'cv_expanding', refused immediately for lstm/gru (T01(c) tabular-only decision) BEFORE any fold fits. Refuses n_splits beyond max_admissible_k as a FIT-TIME BACKSTOP behind /split-stats' own config-time refusal — costs nothing extra (labelled frame already in memory), fires before fold 0. TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=k)'s own cut arithmetic duplicated as expanding_fold_plan (never sklearn's cross_validate, per the advisor-caught correction: that returns fold scores only, never per-fold train_rows/cut_timestamp cv_folds.json requires) — mirrors split_stats_service.py's _expanding_fold_plan exactly, verified index-for-index against a real TimeSeriesSplit (0 mismatches, same measurement T02 cites). k folds fit independently (train+test r2/rmse/mae per fold, fold_model discarded after use), then REFIT as fit k+1 over the FULL labelled frame — that becomes model.joblib; refit_rows recorded in metrics for V03's own assertion. No predictions.parquet written for CV (predictions_path stays None, outputs dict omits the key entirely — not null, absent). Inline holdout scoring (9b) explicitly skipped for CV even when holdoutDataUrl is present, logged plainly, deferred to T07's separate phase. splitSpec's third discriminated-union variant (cv_expanding) added to model-run.authorized.dto.ts in this SAME pass, per finding 7's own instruction — lightweight (cut/row counts only, no metrics) since cv_folds.json (T04) carries the rich per-fold record. VERIFIED: 27/27 images/trainer/test_train.py tests pass (24 pre-existing regression-checked + 3 new for expanding_fold_plan: expanding-and-chronological, cuts-on-labelled-not-row-count (V01 restated for CV), remainder-lands-in-fold-0). A full SMOKE TEST of the actual CV fit loop (real build_model, real sklearn Ridge, real r2/rmse/mae) ran end-to-end against a synthetic sparse-target frame shaped like the real artifacts (32 distinct/8000 rows) — 3 folds fit correctly, refit trained on exactly the labelled total (32 rows), metrics aggregated correctly. 5/5 model-run.authorized.dto.spec.ts tests pass (NEW file — proves V07 directly: a real CV completion payload validates against RunCompleteSchema end-to-end, plus .strict() rejection of a stray chronological-mode field, plus both pre-existing variants still validate unchanged). NOT YET LIVE-RUN: this requires the trainer image to be built and tagged (a Docker build, confirmed with the user before executing — see the feature's own progress_note).

tasks.title: cv_folds.json — per-fold metrics as their own artifact
tasks.detail:
Per fold: its cut timestamp, train and test row counts, distinct labelled count, and train and test r2/rmse/mae. Written under drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/ alongside the run's other artifacts, and registered in the SAME three places every existing run-artifact filename is — train.py's outputs dict, Python's _ALLOWED_RUN_UPLOADS, and the TS RUN_UPLOAD_FILENAMES array. MODEL-FLOW-013-T05's note names all three and states that missing one is how a filename ends up refused at upload; MODEL-FLOW-009-T04 separately had to add a missing COPY line to the Dockerfile for the same class of omission.

A new ModelTrainingRun.cvFoldsKey column, nullable — a non-CV run has none, and a run predating this feature reads as 'not recorded' rather than triggering a reconstruction. That is the honest-legacy-null pattern MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 established for validationMissingPct and MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 reused for frameworkVersions.

BOUNDED: k is already capped by T02, so an oversized artifact is unreachable by construction rather than by a check. State that in the schema comment so a future reader does not add a redundant guard.
tasks.result: cv_folds.json registered in all three required places (MODEL-FLOW-013-T05's own warning about what happens when one is missed): train.py's outputs dict, apps/python's _ALLOWED_RUN_UPLOADS (artifact_service.py), and RUN_UPLOAD_FILENAMES (artifact-keys.ts) — plus the CV_FOLDS_FILENAME constant mirrored in all three of object_store.py/train.py/artifact-keys.ts. Per-fold record: fold index, cut_timestamp, train_rows, test_rows, distinct, r2/rmse/mae AND train_r2/train_rmse/train_mae — written as {algorithm, n_splits, folds: [...]}, matching loss_history.json's own {algorithm, metric, series} top-level convention. MIGRATION APPLIED LIVE to the real dev database (2026-09-01), with a real, pre-existing, UNRELATED drift blocking the normal `prisma migrate dev` flow discovered and worked around without data loss — see the new finding recorded below. Verified via psql: both columns exist on the live ModelTrainingRun table, migration registered in _prisma_migrations with a correct sha256 checksum matching the file. `pnpm db:generate` regenerated the Prisma client and Zod schemas successfully (confirmed: cvFoldsKey present in the generated findFirstModelTrainingRun schema types). complete() sets cvFoldsKey: keyIf('cv_folds.json') — a new backend spec test (model-run.authorized.service.spec.ts) proves both halves: set to the real key when uploaded, null when a non-CV run never uploads it. 12/12 tests pass in that file; full model-run + dataset-version sweep: 135/136 pass (the 1 failure is the pre-existing, unrelated RunTokenGuard DI wiring issue in model-run.authorized.controller.spec.ts, confirmed via git diff to predate this session). Also added scoringContainerId String? in the SAME migration, per this feature's own plan note to bundle T07's scoring-state column rather than author a second migration for one feature.

tasks.title: metrics carries mean AND spread, or CV was pointless
tasks.detail:
A model at rmse 0.6 ± 0.02 and one at 0.6 ± 0.4 are not the same model, and today's schema cannot tell them apart. Storing only a fold mean throws away the one thing k fits were paid for.

MetricsSchema is a bare z.record of scalars, so cv_rmse_mean / cv_rmse_std and their r2/mae siblings validate with no migration — MODEL-FLOW-013-T04 added train_* keys the same way. What does NOT come free is every consumer knowing which number to show, which is T11.

NAME THEM SO NOTHING MISTAKES THEM FOR THE REFIT'S OWN SCORE. They are the configuration's estimate; the refit's own honest number comes from the holdout phase (finding 3) and belongs under different keys. The naming discipline is MODEL-FLOW-013-T04's own: train_* was chosen specifically so nothing would confuse it with holdoutMetrics.
tasks.result: metrics for a CV run carries cv_r2_mean/cv_r2_std and their rmse/mae siblings, plus n_splits and refit_rows — validates against the existing bare z.record(MetricsSchema) with no migration, the same way MODEL-FLOW-013-T04 added train_*. Named cv_* so nothing mistakes these for the refit's own held-out score, which (when it exists) comes from T07's separate holdout-scoring phase — never from these fold statistics. Mean AND spread: cv_r2_std/cv_rmse_std/cv_mae_std are real, computed via np.std across the k fold scores, not placeholders.

tasks.title: A CV run writes no predictions.parquet — and every reader must handle that
tasks.detail:
Per userDecisions: there is no single held-out series under CV, so no file is written and no placeholder is invented. An empty or synthesised predictions file would be worse than its absence — MODEL-FLOW-004 deleted seededNoise/comparePoints/compareFit from this same wizard rather than let a chart fabricate a series to fill space, and MODEL-FLOW-013-T07 carries the same rule for its own charts.

WHAT THIS BREAKS, ENUMERATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: getDraftRunPredictionsService already refuses (404, naming which) a run with no predictionsKey — so the read path is correct as it stands and needs no change. Step 5's four surfaces (actual-vs-predicted, residuals, histogram, Q-Q) all read that one file and must show an honest state pointing at the scoring phase, not an error and not an empty chart. Verify by reading each, not by assuming the shared hook covers them uniformly.

RunCompleteSchema must accept a completion with no predictions key for a CV run specifically. Check whether it currently requires one — the strictness class that produced MODEL-FLOW-009-T04's post-fit 400 lives in exactly this schema.
tasks.result:
TRAINER SIDE DONE: a CV run writes no predictions.parquet — predictions_path stays None, the outputs dict never gains the key (absent, not null). getDraftRunPredictionsService already refuses (404, naming which) a run with no predictionsKey — confirmed unchanged, no code needed there (T01 audit). RunCompleteSchema needs no change for the missing predictions key — T01's audit already established `uploaded` is optional and the .refine() only requires model.joblib (corrected finding, not assumed).

CLOSED OUT by MODEL-FLOW-016-T11 (see that task's own result): all four Step 5 surfaces now show the honest awaiting-scoring/scoring phase for a CV run with no predictionsKey yet, live-verified against a real run's full awaiting->scoring->scored transition.

tasks.title: Holdout scoring as a user-triggered phase after CV
tasks.detail:
The user's own framing, and it closes finding 3's gap rather than merely labelling it: after a CV run terminates, the user selects it and triggers scoring of the REFIT model against the dataset's raw validation holdout. That produces the prediction series and the one honest number the refit can have — the holdout is the only data no fit ever saw.

Reuse replay_holdout_for_run (DS-LAKE-018-T05), which already reads the run's own feature_spec.json rather than having the caller re-supply the recipe, and already refuses a scaled target with no recorded inverse transform. Resolve every key OFF THE RUN ROW, never from the request — the discipline getDraftRunPredictionsService established and mintUploadUrls applies on the write side.

OUTPUT SHAPE IS predictions.parquet's EXISTING SCHEMA (timestamp/y_true/y_pred, confirmed against a real file), written under the same run prefix. That is what keeps MODEL-FLOW-004's four charts working unmodified — a different shape would mean rewriting all of them for a series they can already render.

STATE PLAINLY, EVERYWHERE THE NUMBER APPEARS, that a holdout score is computed on RAW rows: DS-LAKE-018's resolved no-imputation decision means MISSING_VALUE holes reach predict(), so the figure reads LOW for reasons that are not the model's fault. That feature's own T05 already requires the holdout's missing rate be published beside every metric — this is the first consumer that requirement was written for.

PRECONDITION, CHECKED AT CONFIG TIME: a dataset with no holdout cannot reach this phase (finding 6). Refuse CV at Step 3 with the reason named, before k fits are paid for — not at the end, where the user has already spent the time.
tasks.result:
Backend + trainer sides both built, type-clean, unit-tested; NOT yet live-verified (needs the trainer image built/tagged first — same prerequisite T03-T06 already recorded).

DESIGN, refined from the ledger's own detail via an advisor pass before implementation:
- claim() now REFUSES to replay a CV run's holdout inline (new isCvRun gate, model-run.authorized.service.ts) — previously it would have replayed it and handed it to a training container that never reads holdoutDataUrl for CV anyway (train.py's own 9b `and not is_cv` gate). This was a real, previously-undetected double-replay waste this task's own advisor review caught; fixed so the ONE real replay happens at scoring-claim time, not twice.
- Three new endpoints, exactly as designed: POST /authorized/model-drafts/:draftId/runs/:runId/score (user-facing, JWT, draft-scoped only — scoring is surfaced pre-Save-Model from Step 3 Evaluation) mints a FRESH token (training's is already dead), refuses unless SUCCEEDED+cvFoldsKey set+not already scoring+featureSpecKey/modelKey present, does a CHEAP holdout-existence check (no replay) before ever spawning a container, then spawns via TrainningContainerAuthorizedService.spawn(runId, token, 'score'). POST .../:runId/score-claim (container, ScoreTokenGuard) resolves model.joblib + holdout via the SAME tryReplayHoldout() claim() uses (exposed as a new public resolveHoldoutForRun wrapper) plus feature_columns off the manifest, refusing loudly if either is missing — unlike claim()'s own soft-fail for a legitimately-holdout-less non-CV run, a hole here after trigger already checked is a real failure. POST .../:runId/score-complete (container, ScoreTokenGuard) writes ONLY predictionsKey + holdoutMetrics + clears scoringContainerId + closes the token — touches no status/finishedAt/splitSpec/candidate-job nudge, so a re-score can never re-flip a terminal run's own recorded training outcome.
- NEW ScoreTokenGuard (apps/backend/src/guards/score-token.guard.ts), deliberately NOT a reuse of RunTokenGuard: that guard's own terminal-status check (status must be QUEUED/RUNNING) already REFUSES a scoring token on every training route by construction, since a CV run is SUCCEEDED throughout scoring — discovered via an advisor pass BEFORE implementation, which reframed the training-token-reuse risk from 'needs a train.py code-discipline fix' to 'already structurally blocked by the existing guard, PROVIDED status is never touched' (which scoringContainerId's design already guarantees). ScoreTokenGuard instead gates on scoringContainerId being non-null — the same column doing double duty as both the UI's poll target and the auth precondition.
- TrainningContainerAuthorizedService.spawn/watch/reconcileOrphanedRuns parameterized by mode: 'train'|'score' rather than a near-duplicate spawnScore — the HostConfig security settings (CapDrop, ReadonlyRootfs, Tmpfs, memory caps) stay single-sourced. Boot reconcile now ALSO sweeps scoringContainerId != null rows (a gap found during implementation: a restart during scoring would have stranded the flag forever, since status never flips to RUNNING for a scoring container) — 9 tests total, 2 new for this branch.
- train.py: MODE env var (default 'train'), log() now posts to /score-log in score mode (previously would have 401'd silently — the guard rejects but log()'s own except only catches transport errors, not HTTP status), new run_score() entrypoint (score-claim → download+checksum model.joblib → download+checksum holdout → feature-column coverage check → labelled-row filter (same DS-LAKE-023-T03/D4 discipline) → predict → holdout_metrics with the SAME key names as main()'s own inline holdout scoring → predictions.parquet in the EXACT {timestamp,y_true,y_pred} schema MODEL-FLOW-004's charts already render → score-upload-urls → score-complete). __main__ dispatches to run_score() vs main() by MODE, and its crash handler now posts FAILED to score-complete (never /complete) in score mode — the one place a scoring container's own crash could otherwise have corrupted an already-terminal training run's record. Also removed a now-dead branch in main() (a log-only 'holdout available but not scored inline' message) that could never fire once claim() stopped sending holdoutDataUrl for CV runs at all.
- Extracted 3 small shared libs (2+ callers each, per the codebase's own dedup threshold): resolveRunOwner/buildRunKey (lib/model-run-owner.ts), findHoldoutArtifact (lib/holdout-artifact.ts, the cheap-existence-check / full-replay split the advisor pass specified), mintRunToken (lib/mint-run-token.ts).

Also fixed a race in spawn()'s mode==='score' branch (scoringContainerId now written before container.start(), not after — ScoreTokenGuard has no QUEUED-equivalent admitted state the way RunTokenGuard does for training).

COMPLETED THE MISSING RUN-CREATION LINK (2026-09-01, second pass). Found while finishing this task: nSplits was NEVER threaded into run creation — CreateTrainingRunSchema had no such field and buildRunData hard-coded `method: 'chronological'`, so NO CV run could be created at all and this entire scoring phase was unreachable regardless of the trainer image. Neither T03 nor T04 claimed this work (checked their own result fields before assuming an overclaim) — it was simply dropped between the trainer pass and this one. Now: CreateTrainingRunSchema gains `nSplits` (2-10, bounds matching CvExpandingSplitSpecSchema's own n_splits exactly so a run cannot launch at a k its completion callback would reject) with a .refine making it mutually exclusive with trainTestSplit; buildRunData emits {method:'cv_expanding', n_splits} for such a run, leaving source_rows/labelled_rows/distinct_labelled_values and per-fold cuts for the container to fill (same reason cut_timestamp already was: unknowable before non-Good target rows are dropped).

V06 PRECONDITION IMPLEMENTED (this task's own 'PRECONDITION, CHECKED AT CONFIG TIME' requirement, previously deferred): buildRunData now refuses a CV run at creation, BEFORE any container spawns, in two cases — (a) algorithm is lstm/gru (T01(c) tabular-only; train.py keeps its own fit-time backstop), and (b) the dataset has no validation holdout (findHoldoutArtifact), with the reason named in full: a CV run writes no predictions by design, so with no holdout its model could never be scored at all and the user would pay for k+1 fits and receive nothing actionable. tasks.title: Step 4 and Step 5 under CV — three numbers, three meanings, never merged
tasks.detail:
A CV run has a configuration estimate (mean ± std across folds), a refit model, and — after T07 — that model's own holdout score. Showing any one of them as 'the' metric is the category error finding 3 names.

Step 4 (Model Selection): a CV run in a candidate set shows mean ± std, and the spread is comparable across candidates in a way a single split's number is not. Reuse MODEL-FLOW-013's existing render-mode discipline — chosen from a property of the RUN, never from a switch on the algorithm name (T05a's own rule, which exists because a hardcoded list in the client is a second source of truth that drifts).

Step 5 (Evaluation): before scoring, an honest state pointing at the scoring action — not an error, and not four empty charts. After scoring, the existing four surfaces render the holdout series unchanged, with the holdout's own missing rate stated beside every figure (T07).

Add a per-fold table with row counts. The fold that looks worst is usually either the smallest or the one spanning a regime change, and both are findings a reliability engineer can act on — but only if the row counts are on screen beside the metrics.
tasks.result:
COMPLETE, live-verified end-to-end against the real dev stack (a real scored CV run, 1a72bda1-...). Advisor caught a SECOND breakage T06's note did not name: a scored CV run's own `metrics` column has no plain r2/rmse at all (only cv_r2_mean/cv_rmse_mean, the FOLD MEAN) -- so gating only on predictionsKey fixes the un-scored path and then throws on the scored path, pairing a holdout series with a fold-mean scalar. Fixed at the root: use-draft-run-evaluation.ts's fetchEvaluation now branches on run.cvFoldsKey for BOTH decisions -- skip predictions() entirely while predictionsKey is null (returns an honest awaiting-scoring/scoring phase, cvScoringPhaseOf, never an error), and once scored, read r2/rmse from holdoutMetrics (the refit's own honest number) rather than metrics (the configuration's fold mean) or a non-existent metrics.r2. States explicitly this is the configuration's estimate, not the shipped model's own score.

OPEN DECISION, ADDED 2026-09-01 (advisor review of T07): scoring is draft-scoped only (triggerScoringService), and assertDraftWritable refuses a SAVED draft. So a CV run saved without ever being scored can never be scored afterward — the model ships with fold metrics and no holdout number, permanently. This may be the correct product answer (scoring is explicitly a pre-save Evaluation-step action), but it is a DECISION to record here, not a gap to silently accept: either Save Model warns when saving an un-scored CV run, or the ledger states plainly that an un-scored CV save is accepted as-is. Needs a call before this task is implemented, not after.

acceptance_criteria: No fold is drawn at random anywhere; every fold's train window precedes its test window in time.

A CV run writes no predictions.parquet, and every reader of that file shows an honest state rather than an error or an empty chart.

A dataset with no holdout cannot start a CV run.

No Model row is created before Save Model, and ModelDraft gains no column.

features.title: Step 4 — Actual vs Predicted as every candidate's base chart, with its own diagnostic beside it
features.description: Give every candidate in Model Selection the same base chart — actual against predicted over the test split — so candidates are compared on the one view every algorithm can produce. The per-algorithm diagnostic (a loss curve where the estimator iterates, paired train-vs-test marks where it does not) becomes a SECOND chart beside it rather than the only one, so a closed-form algorithm is no longer represented by a chart shape that exists to say it has nothing to show.
userDecisions: ACTUAL VS PREDICTED IS THE BASE, NOT THE ALTERNATIVE (resolved). MODEL-FLOW-013-T07 built loss visualisation as the primary per-candidate view, with mode B (paired marks) as the honest fallback for the seven algorithms that cannot produce a curve. That was correct for what it set out to do and leaves ols/ridge/pls/grp/svm/random_forest — the majority of the catalogue — represented by two dots. Actual-vs-predicted is producible by every algorithm from the artifact each run already writes, so it becomes the common ground and the diagnostic becomes supplementary.

TWO CHARTS PER CANDIDATE, NOT ONE MERGED (resolved). The base answers 'does this model track reality'; the diagnostic answers 'did it converge, and how'. Overlaying a loss trajectory on a value series would put two incompatible y-axes in one frame and imply a relationship between them that does not exist.
findings: STEP 4's CHARTS TODAY ARE MOSTLY A STATEMENT THAT THERE IS NOTHING TO PLOT. MODEL-FLOW-013-T05's own live verification, run against the pinned library versions rather than fakes, established which algorithms actually yield a loss history: ols/ridge/pls/grp/svm/random_forest return None; mlp returns train-only; lightgbm/xgboost return train+validation; and hist_gradient_boosting returns EMPTY ARRAYS for any dataset at or under 10,000 rows — the common case in this trainer's domain — so it too falls to mode B. That is seven of ten algorithms whose entire visual representation in the comparison step is two paired marks. The marks are honest and were the right call; they are not a basis for comparing models.

EVERY CANDIDATE ALREADY HAS THE DATA FOR THE BASE CHART. A SUCCEEDED run writes predictions.parquet under drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/ with schema timestamp/y_true/y_pred — confirmed against a real file (run 61f9aa28: 1,341 rows, three columns, no nulls). Every algorithm writes it, closed-form included, because it is the output of predict() and not a property of the fitting procedure. MODEL-FLOW-004 already built the read path (run_predictions in Python, getDraftRunPredictionsService in NestJS) and both chart components (ActualVsPredictedChart, ResidualChart). This feature is composition of proven parts — which is why its risk sits in payload volume (T02) and not in its panels.

THE READ ROUTE IS DRAFT-RUN-SCOPED AND ITS REACH OVER A CANDIDATE RUN IS UNVERIFIED. GET .../model-drafts/:draftId/runs/:runId/predictions resolves keys off the run row, and a candidate run IS a ModelTrainingRun with the same columns — so it most likely already works. But 'most likely' is what MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found wrong five times out of seven, and MODEL-FLOW-013-T09's whole reason for existing was to stop a later feature being built on the assumption of one run per draft. T01 confirms by calling it against a real candidate run, not by reading the resolver.

FIVE CANDIDATES x A FULL TEST SPLIT IS A PAYLOAD PROBLEM MODEL-FLOW-004 DELIBERATELY DID NOT SOLVE. That feature set MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS=20000 and built NO decimation branch, recording in the schema's own comment that a run over the cap is refused by name rather than silently sampled, and that the design for whoever hits the cap first was deferred. It was sized for ONE chart on ONE run: 1,341 points observed against a 20,000 cap is comfortable. Step 4 renders every candidate at once — five runs of that size is 6,705 points fetched over five requests, and a larger dataset multiplies both. This feature is the caller that hits the deferred design.

DS-LAKE ALREADY SOLVED THE SHAPE OF THIS AND ITS ANSWER DOES NOT TRANSFER UNCHANGED. scatter_service decimates by 2D grid binning explicitly NOT via the LTTB path /preview uses, because a scatter's axes are tag values rather than time. An actual-vs-predicted chart IS time-ordered, so LTTB is the right family here — but the series must be decimated as a PAIR (y_true and y_pred at the same kept timestamps) or the two lines would be sampled at different points and the visible gap between them, which is the entire thing a reader looks at, would become an artefact of sampling.

MODE SELECTION MUST STAY A PROPERTY OF THE RUN. MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a established renderModeFor(candidate) as the single branch site, keyed on whether the run has a lossHistory and never on the algorithm name, precisely so the client holds no membership list to drift when lstm/gru unblock or the catalogue grows. Adding a second chart must not reintroduce a name-keyed branch anywhere — the base chart is unconditional, and only the diagnostic consults that one existing predicate.
openDecisions: SMALL MULTIPLES OR ONE OVERLAID CHART FOR THE BASE VIEW? Per-candidate charts scale to any number and read one at a time; a single chart with actual once and each candidate's prediction as its own series makes divergence directly comparable but becomes unreadable past three or four candidates and needs a colour key that survives a FAILED candidate leaving a gap. MODEL-FLOW-013-T07's existing layout is one row per candidate, so small multiples is the smaller change — recorded rather than assumed, because the overlaid version is the one an engineer comparing two close candidates would actually want.

tasks.title: Audit: can the predictions route serve a candidate run, and what does the payload actually weigh
tasks.detail:
READ AND CALL, DO NOT INFER — MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code, and -004/-005/-006/-012 each opened with an audit that changed their own scope.

Confirm: (a) GET .../model-drafts/:draftId/runs/:runId/predictions returns a real series for a run whose candidateJobId is set, called against a real candidate run rather than reasoned about from the resolver (finding 3); (b) the observed point count per candidate on the largest real dataset available, against MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS=20000 — the 1,341 measured on run 61f9aa28 is one run on one dataset and is not the ceiling; (c) whether Step 4's existing fetch is per-candidate or one call, since five sequential requests on step entry is a different problem from one large one; (d) whether ActualVsPredictedChart and ResidualChart can render at small-multiple size without their axis labels and legends colliding — they were built for one full-width chart.

If (a) comes back refusing a candidate run, T03 gains a route change and this stops being composition.

tasks.title: Decimate paired series for comparison, and say when it happened
tasks.detail:
The deferred design MODEL-FLOW-004 recorded, now that this feature is its first caller (finding 4). LTTB over the time axis, not scatter_service's 2D grid binning — that method exists because a scatter's axes are tag values; this series is time-ordered (finding 5).

DECIMATE THE PAIR AT THE SAME TIMESTAMPS. Sampling y_true and y_pred independently would make the visible gap between the lines an artefact of which points each series happened to keep — and that gap is the only thing a reader is looking at. This is the load-bearing constraint of the whole task.

STATE IT WHERE IT HAPPENED, following the precedent DraftScatterResult already sets: it carries both `points` (decimated) and `n` (the true count) plus a `downsampled` flag, and TagScatterChart renders 'N of M shown; fit uses all M'. Do the same rather than showing a quietly thinned series — a chart that hides its own sampling is one a reader cannot calibrate.

RESIDUAL FIGURES ARE NOT RECOMPUTED FROM THE DECIMATED SERIES. run_predictions computes residual_sd and its residual_rmse_check over the FULL frame; those stay full-frame, exactly as scatter's regression coefficients are fit over the full Good-filtered frame while its plotted cloud is decimated.

tasks.title: One fetch for a candidate set's series, not one per candidate
tasks.detail:
Step 4 needs every terminal candidate's series at once. Five sequential per-run requests on step entry is five artifact reads for one screen — the same argument MODEL-FLOW-014's userDecisions used to reject two /boxplot calls in favour of one /split-stats.

Resolve every key off the job and run rows, never from the request — the discipline getDraftRunPredictionsService established and mintUploadUrls applies on the write side. A PENDING or QUEUED candidate contributes no series and is not an error.

BOUNDED BY CANDIDATE COUNT TOO, not only by points per candidate: CreateCandidateJobSchema caps a set at 20, so twenty decimated series is the real worst case and the per-candidate budget must be set against that, not against a set of five. Refuse an oversized response by name rather than truncating silently, and record the reasoning in the schema's own comment for whoever raises the cap.

CHECK BEFORE BUILDING whether T01(c) found the existing shape already sufficient — if Step 4 already fetches once, this task is smaller than it reads.

tasks.title: Actual vs Predicted as the unconditional base chart per candidate
tasks.detail:
Every terminal candidate gets one, regardless of algorithm — that is the whole point (finding 1). Reuse ActualVsPredictedChart rather than writing a second implementation of the same view; MODEL-FLOW-004 already carries its ±1 SD band and its own doc comment on what the band means.

NO NAME-KEYED BRANCH ANYWHERE (finding 6). The base chart is unconditional; renderModeFor stays the single branch site and is consulted only by T05's diagonstic. A `switch (algorithm)` added here would be the second source of truth MODEL-FLOW-013-T05a exists to prevent, and it would drift toward showing an empty chart rather than an honest one.

A FAILED candidate keeps its row and its reason and shows no chart — it produced no predictions, and an empty chart frame reads as a model that predicted nothing rather than one that never ran. MODEL-FLOW-013-T07 already established that a failed candidate stays listed rather than disappearing; this extends that rule to the chart area.

HONEST STATES, reusing MODEL-FLOW-004's own vocabulary rather than a second set of words for the same conditions: candidate still running, candidate terminal but its predictions unreadable, and — once MODEL-FLOW-016 lands — a CV candidate that has no predictions.parquef at all by design and points at its scoring phase instead.

tasks.title: The per-algorithm diagnostic moves beside the base, unchanged in substance
tasks.detail:
MODEL-FLOW-013-T07's two modes stay exactly as built and verified — mode A's train series with its second series labelled 'Test split' (never 'Validation'), its Y axis labelled from the run's own metric name via modeAMetricLabel rather than assumed RMSE; mode B's paired marks rendered as plain divs with no Line, no path element and no .recharts-wrapper, so a two-point line cannot be faked into a curve. That component and its tests are not rewritten; only its position and its billing change.

WHAT CHANGES IS ITS STATUS. It was the primary view and is now supplementary, which is what makes mode B acceptable rather than thin: two paired marks beside a real actual-vs-predicted series is a supporting detail; two paired marks alone was a candidate's entire representation.

LABEL WHAT EACH CHART ANSWERS, in the UI and not only here. 'Does it track reality' and 'did it converge' are different questions, and a reader given two charts with no framing will assume the second is a refinement of the first.

EPOCH COUNT AND ITERATION COUNT ARE NOT UNIVERSAL AND MUST NOT BE PRINTED AS IF THEY WERE: mlp reports its own loss_curve_ length, lightgbm/xgboost report n_estimators-many rounds, and the seven mode-B algorithms have no iteration concept at all. Read the length from the run's own artifact; never derive it from a hyperparameter the estimator may have stopped short of.

tasks.title: Layout that survives twenty candidates and a mixed set
tasks.detail:
Two charts per candidate against a 20-candidate cap is forty charts. Whatever T01(d) found about small-multiple rendering decides whether both charts sit side by side per row, or the diagnostic is revealed per candidate on demand.

A MIXED SET IS THE NORMAL CASE, not an edge one: an algorithm sweep across ols/ridge/lightgbm/mlp/svm yields two mode-A diagnostics and three mode-B in one screen. The layout must not make a mode-B row look broken next to a mode-A row — they are different answers to the same question, not a complete and an incomplete rendering of one.

MODEL-FLOW-013-T11's phase grouping ('Sweep' / 'Tuning <winner>') already exists and renders only once a phase-2 group is present. This layout sits inside those groups and must not flatten them — a tuning phase's candidates all share one algorithm, so their diagnostics are directly comparable in a way the sweep phase's are not, which is worth preserving visually.

acceptance_criteria: Every terminal candidate shows an actual-vs-predicted chart, whatever its algorithm — no candidate is represented only by paired marks.
The base chart's render path contains no branch on algorithm name; renderModeFor remains the single branch site and governs only the diagnostic.
A decimated series keeps y_true and y_pred sampled at the SAME timestamps, and the chart states that decimation occurred with the true point count.
Residual figures are computed over the full frame, never over the decimated series.
A candidate set is fetched in one request, and the response is bounded against the 20-candidate cap rather than against a typical set size.
A FAILED candidate keeps its row and its reason and shows no empty chart frame.
Each chart says which question it answers.
Iteration or epoch counts come from the run's own artifact, never from a hyperparameter the estimator may not have reached.
A mixed mode-A/mode-B set reads as two kinds of answer, not as one complete and one broken rendering.
Model Selection still creates no Model row and adds no ModelDraft column.

verification.description: PROVE THE BASE CHART IS UNCONDITIONAL: render a candidate set containing a closed-form algorithm (ols or ridge) beside a mode-A one (lightgbm or mlp) and assert BOTH have an actual-vs-predicted chart, while only the second has a loss curve. Asserting only the mode-A candidate would pass against the pre-feature behaviour unchanged.

PROVE PAIRED DECIMATION: decimate a real series and assert every kept y_pred shares a timestamp with a kept y_true, and that the point count and the flag are surfaced. Asserting only the reduced length would pass against two independently sampled series — the exact defect this constraint exists to prevent, and one that would be invisible in the rendered chart.

Assert residual_sd from the decimated response equals the full-frame value, using run 61f9aa28's own recorded 0.435277 as the fixture — a figure MODEL-FLOW-004-V01 already digit-verified against the trainer, so a regression here is measurable rather than a matter of opinion.

Render a set containing a FAILED candidate and confirm it keeps its row and reason with no chart frame, alongside SUCCEEDED candidates that do have charts. Both halves in one render, or the test cannot distinguish correct suppression from a set that happened to contain no failures.

Grep the Step 4 render path for any branch on algorithm name and assert renderModeFor is still the only one — the static-source discipline MODEL-FLOW-012's run-params guard and MODEL-FLOW-010-V02's import guard both already use in this codebase, and the check that stops a membership list reappearing when lstm/gru unblock.

Fetch a 20-candidate set's series and record the real payload size against whatever budget T03 sets. The cap is what makes the bound real; a five-candidate measurement would confirm nothing about the case the schema actually permits.

global_definition_of_done: Serving, promotion and retraining are OUT of this ledger's scope and live in MODEL-SERVE; what this ledger owes them is a saved Model that records its artifact, checksum, feature spec and framework version — nothing downstream re-derives those.
The six-step Model Creation Flow is preserved (MODEL-FLOW-010 went four to five; MODEL-FLOW-013 inserted Model Selection, five to six).
A dataset selected at Step 1 is reviewable at Step 2 before any training is configured.
Step 3 Training Configuration behavior remains unchanged.
Step 6 Save Model behavior remains unchanged.
Training runs without committing the Model to the database.
Evaluation works without a persistent Model database record.
Fine-Tuning runs as a background process.
Fine-Tuning does not commit the Model to the database.
Model configuration is preserved before final Save Model.
Model artifacts are stored and referenced correctly.
Save Model is the only persistence boundary for the final Model.
Failed Save Model operations do not leave partial Model records.
No unrelated functionality is changed or broken.
No persistent MODEL record is created before Save Model. Draft, job and log rows ARE written before it — they are what makes a container able to run and report at all.
Every metric shown in Step 3 comes from a run whose target-leakage guard actually executed.
